claims.source_quote: Each recognition act (signing, declaring, deciding) generates a new dependent continuant inhering in an institutional continuant.
claims.note: Asserts what recognition acts produce and the inherence relation of dependent continuants.

claims.claim: Each institutional continuant persists through time by realizing functions defined by its roles.
claims.source_quote: each institutional continuant persists through time by realizing functions defined by its roles.
claims.note: Asserts how institutional continuants persist and the role of function realization.

claims.claim: Each realization reinforces the network of recognition that sustains the system as a whole.
claims.source_quote: each realization reinforces the network of recognition that sustains the system as a whole.
claims.note: Asserts a causal/sustaining relation between realizations and the recognition network.

claims.claim: Legal facts are continuously regenerated through processes of recognition, realization, and recordkeeping.
claims.source_quote: legal facts are continuously regenerated through processes of recognition, realization, and recordkeeping, a recursive cycle that constitutes the ontology of legal reality.
claims.note: Asserts how legal facts come to exist and persist.

claims.claim: Law creates a parallel layer of reality populated by entities that exist only through structured recognition.
claims.source_quote: Law does not merely describe or regulate the world; it creates a parallel layer of reality populated by entities that exist only through structured recognition.
claims.note: Asserts that law produces a distinct ontological layer of entities.

claims.claim: The layer of legal reality exerts causal and normative effects on the brute world.
claims.source_quote: This layer, once constituted, exerts causal and normative effects on the brute world, it shapes behavior, distributes power, and mediates social life.
claims.note: Asserts causal and normative properties of the layer of legal reality.

claims.claim: Brute facts depend on physical or causal relations; legal facts depend on recognition and institutional coherence.
claims.source_quote: Brute facts depend on physical or causal relations; legal facts depend on recognition and institutional coherence.
claims.note: Asserts the differing dependency relations of brute facts versus legal facts.

claims.claim: The transition from brute to legal fact is an act of structured augmentation adding new relational continuants.
claims.source_quote: The transition from one to the other is not a leap into fiction but an act of structured augmentation: the world becomes more articulated through the addition of new relational continuants.
claims.note: Asserts the nature of the brute-to-legal-fact transition and what it produces.

claims.claim: Law is the organized practice of producing and maintaining augmentations that turn human action into social reality.
claims.source_quote: Law, in this view, is the organized practice of producing and maintaining these augmentations, of turning the flux of human action into the durable architecture of social reality.
claims.note: Asserts what law is as a practice and its function.

claims.claim: Legal facts are realized through processes such as trials, hearings, filings, and administrative procedures.
claims.source_quote: These processes, trials, hearings, filings, and administrative procedures, constitute the ontological machinery through which law transforms events into enduring institutional entities.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological role of procedural processes in realizing legal facts.

claims.claim: Trials, hearings, filings, and administrative procedures are occurrents in BFO terms.
claims.source_quote: In the language of Basic Formal Ontology (BFO), such processes are occurrents: temporally bounded activities that bring about changes in the configuration of continu

claims.claim: A physical deed carries the institutional relation of recognition that constitutes ownership.

claims.claim: Ownership is established by a system of institutional and social recognition, not by documents alone.

claims.claim: Documents are enduring proof of legal status, not the enduring form of the legal fact itself.

claims.note: Asserts a distinction between document and legal fact, giving each a property.

claims.claim: The apparent objectivity of law reflects the genuine endurance of dependent continuants within the institutional field.
claims.source_quote: This appearance is not illusory; it reflects the genuine endurance of dependent continuants within the institutional field.
claims.note: Asserts that dependent continuants genuinely endure within institutional fields.

claims.claim: Law's objectivity arises from the stability of recognition across time, not from metaphysical independence.

claims.note: Asserts the source/property of law's objectivity.

claims.claim: The truth conditions of legal facts depend on the alignment of recognition among institutions.

claims.claim: Law is the organized practice of producing and maintaining augmentations that turn human action into durable social reality.

claims.note: Asserts that legal processes are a subkind of occurrents.

claims.claim: Legal processes constitute the ontological machinery through which law transforms events into enduring institutional entities.
claims.source_quote: These processes, trials, hearings, filings, and administrative procedures, constitute the ontological machinery through which law transforms events into enduring institutional entities.
claims.note: Asserts a functional/constitutive role for legal processes.

claims.claim: The U.S. Constitution persists as a structure of ongoing recognition instantiated in courts, legislatures, and citizens.
claims.source_quote: The U.S. Constitution, for instance, persists not as parchment or memory but as a structure of ongoing recognition instantiated in courts, legislatures, and citizens.
claims.note: Direct assertion about the ontological nature and mode of persistence of a specific legal entity.

claims.claim: The U.S. Constitution's reality lies in the intersubjective fabric that sustains it.
claims.source_quote: Its reality lies in the intersubjective fabric that sustains it.
claims.note: Asserts a property (locus of reality) of a specific entity (the U.S. Constitution).

claims.claim: Recognition is at once moral, social, and behavioral.
claims.source_quote: It is at once moral, social, and behavioral, an act of acknowledgment that carries normative weight, is expressed through collective behavior, and sustains moral order.
claims.note: Asserts multiple properties of the entity 'recognition'.

claims.claim: Recognition carries normative weight.
claims.source_quote: an act of acknowledgment that carries normative weight, is expressed through collective behavior, and sustains moral order.
claims.note: Asserts a property of recognition as an ontological entity.

claims.claim: Recognition sustains moral order.
claims.source_quote: an act of acknowledgment that carries normative weight, is expressed through collective behavior, and sustains moral order.
claims.note: Asserts a functional/relational property of recognition.

claims.claim: Recognition is the foundation and the mode of law's being.
claims.source_quote: Recognition is thus both the foundation and the mode of law's being.
claims.note: Asserts a fundamental ontological role and relation of recognition to law's existence.

claims.claim: A statute's meaning exists in the alignment of recognition that links text and court behavior.
claims.source_quote: A statute's meaning exists not in the text alone nor in the court's behavior but in the alignment of recognition that links the two.
claims.note: Asserts where statutory meaning exists as an ontological matter.

claims.claim: The law in books expresses potential relations.
claims.source_quote: The law in books expresses potential relations; the law in action realizes them.
claims.note: Asserts a property/function of 'law in books' as an ontological entity.

claims.claim: The law in action realizes potential relations.
claims.source_quote: The law in books expresses potential relations; the law in action realizes them.
claims.note: Asserts a property/function of 'law in action' as an ontological entity.

claims.claim: Both 'law in books' and 'law in action' are manifestations of the same relational process.
claims.source_quote: Both are manifestations of the same relational process.
claims.note: Asserts that two kinds of legal phenomena are subkinds or instances of a single relational process.

claims.claim: When recognition becomes fractured or contested, the unity of meaning and validity breaks down.
claims.source_quote: When that framework falters, when recognition becomes fractured or contested, the unity of meaning and validity breaks down.
claims.note: Asserts a relational dependency: the unity of meaning and validity depends on coherent recognition.

claims.claim: The crisis of legal meaning is a crisis of recognition.
claims.source_quote: The crisis of legal meaning, then, is at its core a crisis of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts an identity/constitution relation between two kinds of crisis.

claims.claim: Legal meaning constitutes part of reality itself.
claims.source_quote: Meaning is not imposed upon reality from outside; it constitutes part of reality itself.
claims.note: Asserts that legal meaning is a real part of reality, not merely a subjective overlay.

claims.claim: Legal meaning is structural participation, not subjective interpretation.
claims.source_quote: Legal meaning is not subjective interpretation but structural participation.
claims.note: Asserts a property/nature of legal meaning.

claims.claim: Judges, lawyers, and citizens co-create the ontology of law through acts of understanding.
claims.source_quote: Judges, lawyers, and citizens co-create the ontology of law through acts of understanding that are at once epistemic and existential.
claims.note: Asserts who the agents are that produce the ontological structure of law and how.

claims.claim: Interpretation is the maintenance of law's being, not the discovery of meaning.
claims.source_quote: In this sense, interpretation is not the discovery of meaning but the maintenance of being.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological function/role of interpretation.

claims.claim: Each act of reading, citing, or applying a rule reinforces the recognition that keeps that rule alive.
claims.source_quote: Each act of reading, citing, or applying a rule reinforces the pattern of recognition that keeps that rule alive.
claims.note: Asserts a causal/sustaining relation between interpretive acts and the existence of legal rules.

claims.claim: An invalid law is a failed act of recognition lacking the requisite relational support.
claims.source_quote: An invalid law is not simply a mistaken command but a failed act of recognition, an attempt to create legal being without the requisite relational support.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological nature of legal invalidity.

claims.claim: When an illegitimate authority issues a decree or a statute contradicts higher norms, the failure is ontological.
claims.source_quote: When an illegitimate authority issues a decree, or when a statute contradicts higher norms, the failure is ontological: the entity purports to exist but cannot sustain itself within the network of dependencies.
claims.note: Asserts that certain legal failures are ontological failures of existence.

claims.claim: Nullification and repeal are acts of ontological repair restoring coherence to the structure of recognition.
claims.source_quote: Nullification and repeal, from this standpoint, are acts of ontological repair, restoring coherence to the structure of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological function/role of legal acts of nullification and repeal.

claims.claim: To exist legally is to be coherently recognized.
claims.source_quote: Validity and existence are thus intertwined: to exist legally is to be coherently recognized.
claims.note: Asserts a constitutive condition for legal existence.

claims.claim: Validity and legal existence are intertwined.
claims.source_quote: Validity and existence are thus intertwined: to exist legally is to be coherently recognized.
claims.note: Asserts a relation between validity and existence as ontological categories in law.

claims.claim: Legal institutions are structured continuities of acknowledgment, not arbitrary conventions.
claims.source_quote: The concept of recognition...reveals that legal institutions are not arbitrary conventions but structured continuities of acknowledgment.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological nature/kind of legal institutions.

claims.claim: A law exists when recognized by those authorized to recognize it within a structure existing by virtue of shared recognition.
claims.source_quote: A law exists when it is recognized by those authorized to recognize it, within a structure that itself exists by virtue of shared recognition.
claims.note: Asserts the conditions for the existence of a law as an ontological matter.

claims.claim: Law is the ongoing realization of recognition at multiple levels.
claims.source_quote: This recursive relation is the ontological core of legality: law is the ongoing realization of recognition at multiple levels.
claims.note: Asserts the fundamental nature/identity of law in ontological terms.

claims.claim: The legal world is populated by structures of dependence between agents, roles, roles and institutions, and obligations and acts of recognition.
claims.source_quote: What kinds of entities populate the legal world?...The answers lie not in texts or motives but in structures of dependence, between agents and roles, roles and institutions, obligations and acts of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts what kinds of entities exist in the legal world and their relational structure.

claims.claim: Law's meaning is a mode of being sustained through relation.
claims.source_quote: Law's meaning, in this view, is neither an interpretive product nor a moral essence but a mode of being sustained through relation.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological nature of legal meaning.

claims.claim: Law is a real system of socially sustained meanings operating through acts of recognition woven into institutional life.
claims.source_quote: Law is not an illusion or an ideal but a real system of socially sustained meanings, one that operates through acts of recognition woven into the fabric of institutional life.
claims.note: Asserts that law is a real entity of a specific kind with specific properties and mode of operation.

claims.claim: Roles, obligations, and institutions form the architecture of law as a structured domain of social reality.
claims.source_quote: to map how roles, obligations, and institutions form the architecture of law as a structured domain of social reality.
claims.note: Asserts a structural/compositional relation, though framed as a project goal; the author commits to this as a description of law's ontological structure.

claims.claim: Trials, hearings, filings, and administrative procedures are the ontological machinery through which law transforms events into enduring institutional entities.
claims.source_quote: These processes, trials, hearings, filings, and administrative procedures, constitute the ontological machinery through which law transforms events into enduring institutional entities.
claims.note: Direct assertion that these processes have the ontological function of transforming events into institutional entities.

claims.claim: Processes such as trials and hearings are occurrents in the BFO sense: temporally bounded activities that bring about changes in continuants.
claims.source_quote: In the language of Basic Formal Ontology (BFO), such processes are occurrents: temporally bounded activities that bring about changes in the configuration of continuants.
claims.note: Author positively asserts that these legal processes are occurrents and defines their nature as temporally bounded activities affecting continuants.

claims.claim: These processes are mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities.
claims.source_quote: They are the mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities, turning the abstract conditions of recognition into concrete instances of legal facticity.
claims.note: Asserts a functional/relational property of the processes: they actualize potentialities.

claims.claim: These processes turn abstract conditions of recognition into concrete instances of legal facticity.
claims.source_quote: They are the mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities, turning the abstract conditions of recognition into concrete instances of legal facticity.
claims.note: Asserts a transformative relation: abstract conditions become concrete legal facts through these processes.

claims.claim: The procedural realization of facts bridges law's dynamic and static dimensions.
claims.source_quote: The procedural realization of facts is thus the bridge between law's dynamic and static dimensions, between the lived temporality of adjudication and the enduring reality of institutional record.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property of procedural realization: it connects dynamic and static dimensions of law.

claims.claim: Adjudication has a lived temporality, while institutional records have an enduring reality.
claims.source_quote: between the lived temporality of adjudication and the enduring reality of institutional record.
claims.note: Implicitly asserts distinct ontological properties of adjudication (temporal) and institutional records (enduring).

claims.claim: Law is a framework for being-together, a structured field of interdependence.
claims.source_quote: law is a framework for being-together, a structured field of interdependence in which individual and institutional existence are mutually constituted.
claims.note: Direct assertion about the nature of law as a relational structure.

claims.claim: Individual and institutional existence are mutually constituted.
claims.source_quote: a structured field of interdependence in which individual and institutional existence are mutually constituted.
claims.note: Asserts a constitutive relation between individuals and institutions.

claims.claim: Institutions are the primary loci of relational structure.
claims.source_quote: Institutions are the primary loci of this relational structure.
claims.note: Asserts a property/role of institutions.

claims.claim: Institutions are enduring complexes of roles, functions, and norms.
claims.source_quote: They are not static entities or legal fictions, but enduring complexes of roles, functions, and norms.
claims.note: Asserts what kind of entity institutions are.

claims.claim: Institutions are not static entities or legal fictions.
claims.source_quote: They are not static entities or legal fictions, but enduring complexes of roles, functions, and norms.
claims.note: Denies a competing ontological classification of institutions.

claims.claim: Judges, clerks, litigants, and jurors bear institutionally defined roles that together realize the court's function of adjudication.
claims.source_quote: judges, clerks, litigants, and jurors each bear institutionally defined roles that together realize the court's function of adjudication.
claims.note: Asserts that roles realize a function—a realization relation claim.

claims.claim: Institutions are continuants that endure by maintaining internal coherence among dependent entities.
claims.source_quote: institutions are continuants that endure by maintaining internal coherence among dependent entities, obligations, permissions, and authorities, that inhere in participants through recognition.
claims.note: Asserts institutions are a subkind of continuant with a persistence condition.

claims.claim: Obligations, permissions, and authorities inhere in participants through recognition.
claims.source_quote: institutions are continuants that endure by maintaining internal coherence among dependent entities, obligations, permissions, and authorities, that inhere in participants through recognition.
claims.note: Asserts an inherence relation between normative entities and participants.

claims.claim: Institutions exist as patterns of interaction sustained by acknowledgment, not as autonomous substances.
claims.source_quote: Their architecture is relational: they exist as patterns of interaction sustained by acknowledgment, not as autonomous substances.
claims.note: Asserts what kind of entity institutions are and denies substance status.

claims.claim: Recognition is the condition of institutional being.
claims.source_quote: Recognition is therefore the condition of institutional being.
claims.note: Asserts a necessary condition for the existence of institutions.

claims.claim: A judge's authority derives from a collectively upheld practice of acknowledgment.
claims.source_quote: A judge's authority does not stem from physical control or personal charisma, but from a collectively upheld practice of acknowledgment that confers legitimacy upon her acts.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological source of judicial authority.

claims.claim: Recognition is the mechanism by which roles and institutions are instantiated.
claims.source_quote: Ontologically, such recognition is the mechanism by which roles and institutions are instantiated.
claims.note: Asserts a causal-ontological relation: recognition instantiates roles and institutions.

claims.claim: When recognition collapses, institutions disintegrate as structural realities.
claims.source_quote: When recognition collapses, when citizens cease to treat judgments as binding or officials cease to regard laws as valid, the institution disintegrates. Its buildings and documents may remain, but its structural reality dissolves.
claims.note: Asserts a necessary condition for institutional existence.

claims.claim: Obligations are real, dependent continuants that constrain action.
claims.source_quote: These expectations are not reducible to moral feelings or social customs; they are instantiated as real, dependent continuants that constrain action.
claims.note: Asserts that obligations are a kind of real dependent continuant.

claims.claim: An obligation persists until fulfilled, extinguished, or nullified by a legitimate authority.
claims.source_quote: An obligation, once created, persists until fulfilled, extinguished, or nullified by a legitimate authority.
claims.note: Asserts a persistence condition and termination conditions for obligations.

claims.claim: Law converts momentary acts of recognition into enduring structures of trust.
claims.source_quote: Through obligation, law converts momentary acts of recognition into enduring structures of trust.
claims.note: Asserts a transformative ontological function of law.

claims.claim: Institutions can endure despite turnover in their participants.
claims.source_quote: The result is a form of social being that endures despite turnover in its participants, a form of institutional immortality grounded in relational continuity.
claims.note: Asserts a property of institutional continuity.

claims.claim: Institutional durability arises from recursive reinforcement between recognition and obligation.
claims.source_quote: Their durability arises from the recursive reinforcement between these two forces. Recognition generates obligations, and the fulfillment of obligations reinforces recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a relational mechanism explaining institutional persistence.

claims.claim: Ontological contradiction is a breakdown in the network of dependencies constituting an institution.
claims.source_quote: Ontologically, contradiction appears as a breakdown in the network of dependencies that constitutes the institution.
claims.note: Asserts what ontological contradiction is in the legal-institutional context.

claims.claim: Repair mechanisms in legal systems are ontological operations that reestablish constitutive relations.
claims.source_quote: These mechanisms are not merely procedural; they are ontological operations that reestablish the relations upon which the institution depends.
claims.note: Asserts a property/function of repair mechanisms as ontological, not merely procedural.

claims.claim: Contradiction debt is the structural burden created when conflicts within a system remain unresolved.
claims.source_quote: I describe this phenomenon as the accumulation of contradiction debt: the structural burden created when conflicts within the system remain unresolved.
claims.note: Author introduces and asserts this ontological concept in his own voice.

claims.claim: Institutions carry contradiction debt until it is repaid through repair or discharged through collapse.
claims.source_quote: Institutions carry this debt until it is repaid through repair or discharged through collapse.
claims.note: Asserts a property of institutions regarding contradiction debt.

claims.claim: A legal system that cannot repair itself eventually ceases to exist as law.
claims.source_quote: A system that can repair itself without losing coherence preserves its identity; one that cannot eventually ceases to exist as law.
claims.note: Asserts a necessary condition for a system's continued existence as law.

claims.claim: Legal institutions persist because they possess both the stability of structure and the flexibility of self-correction.
claims.source_quote: Legal institutions persist because they possess both the stability of structure and the flexibility of self-correction.
claims.note: Asserts properties that explain the persistence of legal institutions.

claims.claim: Justice is a form of ontological balance in which recognition and obligation remain coherent and self-sustaining.
claims.source_quote: justice itself may be understood as a form of ontological balance. A just institution is one whose architecture of recognition and obligation remains coherent and self-sustaining.
claims.note: Author asserts this as his ontological account of justice, though introduced with 'may be understood as.'

claims.claim: Injustice arises when recognition is denied or obligations are imposed asymmetrically.
claims.source_quote: Injustice arises when recognition is denied or obligations are imposed asymmetrically, creating structural contradictions that threaten collapse.
claims.note: Asserts structural conditions for injustice.

claims.claim: Justice is a measure of the health of relational being, not merely a moral ideal.
claims.source_quote: Thus, justice is not merely a moral ideal but a measure of the health of relational being.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological nature of justice.

claims.claim: Law is a network of interdependent entities that arise through recognition, obligation, and institutional participation.
claims.source_quote: law is not simply a body of norms or conventions but a structured domain of social being, a network of interdependent entities that arise through recognition, obligation, and institutional participation.
claims.note: Central ontological claim about the nature of law.

claims.claim: Law is a structured domain of social being.
claims.source_quote: law is not simply a body of norms or conventions but a structured domain of social being
claims.note: Asserts what kind of entity law is.

claims.claim: Processes such as trials, hearings, filings, and administrative procedures constitute the ontological machinery through which law transforms events into enduring institutional entities.
claims.source_quote: These processes, trials, hearings, filings, and administrative procedures, constitute the ontological machinery through which law transforms events into enduring institutional entities.
claims.note: Direct assertion that these processes have the ontological function of transforming events into institutional entities.

claims.claim: Processes are occurrents: temporally bounded activities that bring about changes in the configuration of continuants.
claims.source_quote: In the language of Basic Formal Ontology (BFO), such processes are occurrents: temporally bounded activities that bring about changes in the configuration of continuants.
claims.note: The author asserts the subkind relation (processes are occurrents) and the property of being temporally bounded, adopting BFO's ontological framework.

claims.claim: These processes are mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities.
claims.source_quote: They are the mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities, turning the abstract conditions of recognition into concrete instances of legal facticity.
claims.note: Author asserts a causal/functional role: these processes bear the relation of being the mechanism of actualization of potentialities.

claims.claim: Abstract conditions of recognition are turned into concrete instances of legal facticity through these processes.
claims.source_quote: turning the abstract conditions of recognition into concrete instances of legal facticity.
claims.note: Asserts that legal facticity exists as concrete instances and that processes realize them from abstract conditions.

claims.claim: Procedural realization of facts is the bridge between law's dynamic and static dimensions.
claims.source_quote: The procedural realization of facts is thus the bridge between law's dynamic and static dimensions, between the lived temporality of adjudication and the enduring reality of institutional record.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property: procedural realization mediates between two ontological dimensions of law.

claims.claim: Law has both a dynamic dimension (lived temporality of adjudication) and a static dimension (enduring reality of institutional record).
claims.source_quote: between law's dynamic and static dimensions, between the lived temporality of adjudication and the enduring reality of institutional record.
claims.note: Implied by the author's own framing; asserts that these two dimensions exist and are distinct aspects of law.

claims.claim: Institutional records have enduring reality.
claims.source_quote: the enduring reality of institutional record.
claims.note: Author directly attributes the property of enduring reality to institutional records.

claims.claim: Natural law, positivism, and realism fail to explain law's mode of existence.
claims.source_quote: The introduction situates the discussion within the failures of natural law, positivism, and realism to explain law's mode of existence.
claims.note: The author asserts a property (failure) of these three traditions with respect to an ontological task, indicating a positive claim about their inadequacy.

claims.claim: Legal systems are organized continuities of recognition and obligation.
claims.source_quote: It then articulates the need for a structural realist approach that treats legal systems as organized continuities of recognition and obligation.
claims.note: Although framed as what the approach 'treats' legal systems as, the author endorses this characterization as part of the book's own framework, making it an ontological claim about the nature of legal systems.

claims.claim: Law is structured being-with.
claims.source_quote: It concludes by defining law as structured being-with, a term that encapsulates its relational ontology.
claims.note: The author explicitly defines law as structured being-with and endorses this as capturing law's relational ontology—a direct ontological claim about what kind of thing law is.

claims.claim: Law has a relational ontology.
claims.source_quote: a term that encapsulates its relational ontology.
claims.note: The author asserts that law possesses a relational ontology, a direct property claim about law's mode of being.

claims.claim: Law is a system of relations, not a collection of discrete rules or acts.
claims.source_quote: law is not a collection of discrete rules or acts, but a system of relations. Its meaning and validity depend on the underlying relational forms that connect persons, norms, and institutions.
claims.note: Direct assertion about the nature of law as a kind of entity/structure.

claims.claim: Law's meaning and validity depend on relational forms connecting persons, norms, and institutions.
claims.source_quote: Its meaning and validity depend on the underlying relational forms that connect persons, norms, and institutions.
claims.note: Asserts a dependence relation between law's properties and underlying relational forms.

claims.claim: Recognition is a relational phenomenon involving at least two agents and a shared object.
claims.source_quote: recognition itself is relational, it involves at least two agents and a shared object of acknowledgment.
claims.note: Asserts a structural property of recognition as an entity/relation.

claims.claim: Legal validity depends on a network of dependencies among legislators, courts, and citizens.
claims.source_quote: When we say that a law is 'valid,' we invoke a network of dependencies: between legislators and their procedures, between courts and the texts they interpret, between citizens and the authorities they obey.
claims.note: Asserts ontological dependence relations constituting legal validity.

claims.claim: Dependencies between legislators, courts, and citizens are ontological conditions for law's existence.
claims.source_quote: These dependencies are not merely sociological; they are ontological conditions for law's existence.
claims.note: Explicit assertion that these relations are ontological conditions of existence.

claims.claim: Law is a structure, a pattern of relational continuities holding together diverse agents and acts.
claims.source_quote: Law is thus not a substance but a structure, a pattern of relational continuities that holds together diverse agents and acts.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological category of law (structure, not substance).

claims.claim: A contract is a dependent continuant that persists until fulfilled or extinguished.
claims.source_quote: This recognition generates an enduring relation, a dependent continuant, that persists until fulfilled or extinguished.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological kind (dependent continuant) and persistence property of contracts.

claims.claim: A contract's binding force lies in mutual recognition of obligations and rights, not in physical documents or mental states.
claims.source_quote: its binding force does not lie in ink or paper, nor even in the mental states of the parties, but in the mutual recognition of obligations and rights.
claims.note: Asserts what grounds the binding-force property of contracts.

claims.claim: Statutes and judgments are information artifacts that record and transmit meaning.
claims.source_quote: Some entities, like statutes or judgments, are information artifacts, documents that record and transmit meaning.
claims.note: Classifies statutes and judgments as a subkind (information artifacts) with a function.

claims.claim: Institutions and offices are continuants that persist through time.
claims.source_quote: Others, like institutions and offices, are continuants, structures that persist through time.
claims.note: Classifies institutions and offices as continuants (an ontological category).

claims.claim: Trials and legislative sessions are occurrents through which legal reality is realized.
claims.source_quote: Still others, like trials or legislative sessions, are occurrents, events through which legal reality is realized.
claims.note: Classifies trials and legislative sessions as occurrents (an ontological category).

claims.claim: A law's meaning depends on its recognition by officials.
claims.source_quote: A law's meaning depends on its recognition by officials; an obligation depends on the continued existence of the institution that issued it.
claims.note: Asserts a dependence relation between a law's meaning and official recognition.

claims.claim: An obligation depends on the continued existence of the institution that issued it.
claims.source_quote: an obligation depends on the continued existence of the institution that issued it; an institution depends on recurring processes that renew its legitimacy.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological dependence relation for obligations.

claims.claim: An institution depends on recurring processes that renew its legitimacy.
claims.source_quote: an institution depends on recurring processes that renew its legitimacy.
claims.note: Asserts a dependence relation for institutions on processes.

claims.claim: In BFO terms, an independent entity such as a person or institution can exist on its own.
claims.source_quote: An independent entity, such as a person or institution, can exist on its own; a dependent entity, such as an obligation or right, exists only because certain relations among independent entities obtain.
claims.note: Author endorses this ontological classification in his own framework.

claims.claim: An obligation or right is a dependent entity that exists only because certain relations among independent entities obtain.
claims.source_quote: a dependent entity, such as an obligation or right, exists only because certain relations among independent entities obtain.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological category and dependence condition for obligations and rights.

claims.claim: A right depends on its holder.
claims.source_quote: A right depends on its holder; an office depends on the institution that defines it; an obligation depends on the recognition of both debtor and creditor.
claims.note: Asserts a specific ontological dependence relation for rights.

claims.claim: An office depends on the institution that defines it.
claims.source_quote: an office depends on the institution that defines it
claims.note: Asserts an ontological dependence relation for offices.

claims.claim: An obligation depends on the recognition of both debtor and creditor.
claims.source_quote: an obligation depends on the recognition of both debtor and creditor.
claims.note: Asserts a specific ontological dependence relation for obligations.

claims.claim: Legal entities are dependent continuants that can survive the turnover of individuals and the passage of time.
claims.source_quote: Because legal entities are dependent continuants, they can survive the turnover of individuals and the passage of time.
claims.note: Classifies legal entities as dependent continuants and asserts their persistence property.

claims.claim: The office of 'judge' persists even as judges come and go.
claims.source_quote: The office of 'judge' persists even as judges come and go; the obligation created by a contract persists until it is fulfilled; the constitution endures through countless interpretations.
claims.note: Asserts a persistence property of the office-kind as an individual example.

claims.claim: The obligation created by a contract persists until it is fulfilled.
claims.source_quote: the obligation created by a contract persists until it is fulfilled
claims.note: Asserts a persistence property of contractual obligations.

claims.claim: Law's endurance is an emergent property of the network of dependencies that sustains it.
claims.source_quote: Law's endurance is structural, not personal. It is an emergent property of the network of dependencies that sustains it.
claims.note: Asserts that law's endurance is an emergent property of its relational network.

claims.claim: A court's ruling modifies the network of dependencies by creating or dissolving relations of obligation and right.
claims.source_quote: A court's ruling does not merely predict future behavior; it modifies the network of dependencies by creating or dissolving relations of obligation and right.
claims.note: Asserts that a court ruling has a specific relational effect on the ontological network.

claims.claim: Invalidity is an ontological failure: a disruption in the pattern of dependence.
claims.source_quote: Invalidity, conversely, is a form of ontological failure: a disruption in the pattern of dependence.
claims.note: Asserts what invalidity is as an ontological phenomenon.

claims.claim: A usurped office, unconstitutional statute, or contradictory judgment is ontologically incoherent because its dependencies do not hold together.
claims.source_quote: A usurped office, an unconstitutional statute, or a contradictory judgment are not merely wrong in the normative sense, they are incoherent in the ontological sense. Their dependencies do not hold together.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological property (incoherence) of specific legal entities due to failed dependencies.

claims.claim: A law is valid when the dependencies among recognition, authority, and procedure form a coherent structure.
claims.source_quote: It is valid when those relations align, when the dependencies among recognition, authority, and procedure form a coherent structure.
claims.note: Asserts the conditions for legal validity in ontological terms.

claims.claim: When we say a law 'binds,' we are describing a structural relation, not a moral one.
claims.source_quote: When we say that a law 'binds,' we are describing a structural relation, not a mora[l one].
claims.note: Asserts the ontological category of the binding relation in law.

claims.claim: Law's continuity depends on the interplay of change and coherence within its relational architecture.
claims.source_quote: law's continuity depends on the interplay of change and coherence within its relational architecture.
claims.note: Direct assertion about what law's continuity depends on — a relational/structural ontological claim.

claims.claim: Dependence relations explain the normative dimension of law without reducing it to morality.
claims.source_quote: Dependence relations likewise explain the normative dimension of law without reducing it to morality.
claims.note: Asserts a property/function of dependence relations with respect to law's normative dimension.

claims.claim: Bindingness is a structural relation, not a moral feeling.
claims.source_quote: When we say that a law 'binds,' we are describing a structural relation, not a moral feeling.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological kind of bindingness — it is a structural relation.

claims.claim: Bindingness arises from the configuration of recognition and obligation that connects agents to institutions.
claims.source_quote: Bindingness arises from the configuration of recognition and obligation that connects agents to institutions.
claims.note: Asserts the origin and constitutive basis of bindingness — an ontological claim about what produces it.

claims.claim: The existence of the binding relation between agents and institutions is ontological.
claims.source_quote: Moral judgment may inform whether such bindingness is justified, but the existence of the relation itself is ontological.
claims.note: Explicitly asserts that the relation's existence is ontological, distinguishing it from moral justification.

claims.claim: Law binds because it is part of a structure that makes binding possible.
claims.source_quote: The law binds because it is part of a structure that makes binding possible.
claims.note: Asserts that law bears a part-of relation to a structure, and that this structure has the property of making binding possible.

claims.claim: Procedures are the mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities in law.
claims.source_quote: They are the mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities, turning the abstract conditions of recognition into concrete instances of legal facticity.
claims.note: Direct ontological assertion about the functional role of procedures in actualizing potentialities.

claims.claim: Procedural realization is the bridge between law's dynamic and static dimensions.
claims.source_quote: The procedural realization of facts is thus the bridge between law's dynamic and static dimensions, between the lived temporality of adjudication and the enduring reality of institutional record.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property of procedural realization connecting two ontological dimensions of law.

claims.claim: Law's ontology demands procedures.
claims.source_quote: Every legal system relies on procedures because law's ontology demands them.
claims.note: Direct assertion that law's ontological nature necessitates procedures.

claims.claim: Recognition alone is insufficient to create durable legal entities.
claims.source_quote: Recognition alone is insufficient to create durable entities; it must be expressed, recorded, and stabilized through processes that distribute acknowledgment across agents and time.
claims.note: Ontological claim about the insufficiency of recognition by itself for creating enduring entities.

claims.claim: Legal facts would remain fleeting intentions without procedures.
claims.source_quote: In their absence, legal facts would remain fleeting intentions rather than enduring components of the legal world.
claims.note: Asserts a property difference between procedurally realized and unrealized legal facts.

claims.claim: A verdict, judgment, or deed achieves its ontological status only through a procedural framework.
claims.source_quote: A verdict, a judgment, or a deed achieves its ontological status only when it is processed through a procedural framework that integrates it into the system's memory.
claims.note: Asserts a dependency relation: legal entities depend on procedural frameworks for their ontological status.

claims.claim: Procedure is the temporal realization of law's structural being.
claims.source_quote: Thus, procedure is not ancillary to substance; it is the temporal realization of law's structural being.
claims.note: Direct ontological assertion about the nature and role of procedure in law.

claims.claim: Procedural realization involves the realization of dependent continuants through occurrents.
claims.source_quote: The procedural realization of facts involves two primary relations: the realization of dependent continuants (functions, obligations, roles) through occurrents.
claims.note: Asserts a realization relation between dependent continuants and occurrents.

claims.claim: Procedural realization involves the creation of new dependent continuants that persist after the process concludes.
claims.source_quote: The realization of dependent continuants (functions, obligations, roles) through occurrents, and the creation of new dependent continuants (records, rights, decisions) that persist after the process concludes.
claims.note: Asserts that procedures create new persistent dependent continuants.

claims.claim: A trial is an occurrent that realizes the function of adjudication.
claims.source_quote: A trial, for example, realizes the function of adjudication inherent in the judicial institution. It is an occurrent that brings into being new continuants, judgments, findings, sentences.
claims.note: Asserts that a trial is an occurrent and that it bears a realization relation to the function of adjudication.

claims.claim: Judgments, findings, and sentences are continuants that endure as parts of the legal system.
claims.source_quote: It is an occurrent that brings into being new continuants, judgments, findings, sentences, that endure as parts of the legal system.
claims.note: Asserts that judgments, findings, and sentences are continuants and are parts of the legal system.

claims.claim: Filing a petition realizes the role-based function of initiating adjudication.
claims.source_quote: The act of filing a petition realizes the role-based function of initiating adjudication and creates a new legal continuant: the case file.
claims.note: Asserts a realization relation between filing and a role-based function.

claims.claim: The case file is a new legal continuant and an informational artifact.
claims.source_quote: Creates a new legal continuant: the case file, an informational artifact that embodies the existence of a dispute within the institutional structure.
claims.note: Asserts that a case file is both a legal continuant and an informational artifact.

claims.claim: A trial is a complex occurrent that realizes multiple functions while producing enduring entities.
claims.source_quote: The trial, in its entirety, is thus a complex occurrent that realizes multiple functions while producing enduring entities.
claims.note: Asserts a kind membership and functional property of trials as ontological entities.

claims.claim: Evidence submitted in a trial becomes a recognized evidential entity, a dependent continuant.
claims.source_quote: The submission of evidence transforms physical artifacts or testimony into recognized evidential entities, dependent continuants that exist only within the trial's field of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts that evidential entities are dependent continuants existing within the trial's field of recognition.

claims.claim: The final judgment is a generative event that brings into being new legal facts.
claims.source_quote: The final judgment is not merely a conclusion; it is a generative event that brings into being new legal facts, rights affirmed, obligations imposed, statuses changed.
claims.note: Asserts the generative ontological function of a judgment as an event type.

claims.claim: A rendered judgment becomes a continuant persisting as precedent, record, and enforceable norm.
claims.source_quote: Once rendered, the judgment becomes a continuant that persists through the institutional system as precedent, record, and enforceable norm.
claims.note: Asserts that a judgment is a continuant with the properties of precedent, record, and enforceable norm.

claims.claim: The trial creates legal facts through regulated processes of recognition and validation.
claims.source_quote: It does not simply discover facts but creates legal facts through regulated processes of recognition and validation.
claims.note: Ontological claim distinguishing fact-discovery from fact-creation as the trial's primary function.

claims.claim: Factual truth pertains to correspondence with the brute world.
claims.source_quote: The distinction between factual truth and legal truth is therefore structural: factual truth pertains to correspondence with the brute world, while legal truth pertains to coherence within the network of recognition produced by procedural realization.
claims.note: Asserts a property of factual truth as correspondence-based.

claims.claim: Legal truth pertains to coherence within the network of recognition produced by procedural realization.
claims.source_quote: Legal truth pertains to coherence within the network of recognition produced by procedural realization.
claims.note: Asserts a defining property of legal truth as coherence-based within a procedurally produced network.

claims.claim: A verdict contradicting empirical reality can still constitute a valid legal fact if procedural dependencies are satisfied.
claims.source_quote: A verdict that contradicts empirical reality can still constitute a valid legal fact if it satisfies procedural and institutional dependencies.
claims.note: Asserts a condition sufficient for legal fact-hood, independent of empirical correspondence.

claims.claim: Legal facts operate on a level of dependence defined by procedures rather than physical causality.
claims.source_quote: Legal facts do not compete with natural facts; they operate on a different level of dependence, one defined by procedures rather than physical causality.
claims.note: Asserts a distinguishing ontological property of legal facts regarding their mode of dependence.

claims.claim: Legal facts do not compete with natural facts.
claims.source_quote: Legal facts do not compete with natural facts; they operate on a different level of dependence.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological independence between the domains of legal and natural facts.

claims.claim: Filing transforms an intention or claim into an institutional entity by embedding it in a system of record.
claims.source_quote: The act of filing transforms an intention or claim into an institutional entity by embedding it in a system of record.
claims.note: Asserts a transformative ontological function of filing as an occurrent.

claims.claim: The case entry created by filing is a new continuant that is part of the court's institutional ontology.
claims.source_quote: Jointly create a new continuant, the case entry, which becomes part of the court's institutional ontology. This entity persists even if the complaint is later dismissed or withdrawn.
claims.note: Asserts that the case entry is a continuant and a part of the court's institutional ontology.

claims.claim: The case entry persists even if the complaint is later dismissed or withdrawn.
claims.source_quote: This entity persists even if the complaint is later dismissed or withdrawn.
claims.note: Asserts a persistence property of the case entry continuant.

claims.claim: The case file is an information artifact that contains representations of dependent continuants.
claims.source_quote: The case file, as an information artifact, is the vessel through which recognition achieves material endurance. It contains representations of other dependent continuants, obligations, rights, procedural steps.
claims.note: Asserts that the case file is an information artifact with the function of containing representations of dependent continuants.

claims.claim: Each subsequent filing modifies the ontology of the dispute.
claims.source_quote: Each subsequent filing modifies the structure of this artifact, updating the ontology of the dispute.
claims.note: Asserts that filings bear a modification relation to the ontological structure of the dispute.

claims.claim: Information artifacts are the physical or digital substrates that carry dependent continuants.
claims.source_quote: They are the physical or digital substrates that carry dependent continuants, texts, signatures, seals, data entries, that materialize institutional recognition.
claims.note: Asserts that information artifacts are a kind of substrate bearing dependent continuants.

claims.claim: Information artifacts are independent continuants bearing information content entities (ICEs).
claims.source_quote: Within BFO, these artifacts are independent continuants bearing information content entities (ICEs).
claims.note: Asserts that information artifacts are independent continuants and that they bear ICEs.

claims.claim: An ICE is a generically dependent continuant.
claims.source_quote: An ICE is a generically dependent continuant that can exist on multiple bearers.
claims.note: Asserts a kind membership: ICEs are generically dependent continuants.

claims.claim: An ICE can exist on multiple bearers.
claims.source_quote: An ICE is a generically dependent continuant that can exist on multiple bearers, such as the same statute stored in different media.
claims.note: Asserts a multiplicity property of ICEs regarding their bearers.

claims.claim: Statutes, contracts, verdicts, and records are ICEs in law.
claims.source_quote: In law, ICEs include statutes, contracts, verdicts, and records.
claims.note: Asserts that specific legal entities are instances or kinds of ICEs.

claims.claim: ICEs are the vehicles by which recognition is externalized, preserved, and transmitted in law.
claims.source_quote: They are the vehicles of legal facticity: the means by which recognition is externalized, preserved, and transmitted.
claims.note: Asserts a functional property of ICEs in the legal domain.

claims.claim: A procedural act is an occurrent through which a legal fact is created.
claims.source_quote: Occurrent: The procedural act (trial, filing, enactment) through which a fact is created.
claims.note: Asserts that procedural acts are occurrents with a generative relation to legal facts.

claims.claim: A right, obligation, or decision is a dependent continuant generated by a procedural act.
claims.source_quote: Dependent Continuant: The legal relation or status generated (right, obligation, decision).
claims.note: Asserts that rights, obligations, and decisions are dependent continuants.

claims.claim: An information artifact is the material or digital bearer that embodies the dependent continuant.
claims.source_quote: Information Artifact: The material or digital bearer that embodies the dependent continuant.
claims.note: Asserts a bearing relation between information artifacts and dependent continuants.

claims.claim: An institutional continuant is the system that maintains recognition of the information artifact.
claims.source_quote: Institutional Continuant: The system (court, registry, agency) that maintains recognition of the artifact.
claims.note: Asserts that courts, registries, and agencies are institutional continuants with a recognition-maintaining function.

claims.claim: Law is a structured form of being-with, embodying a relational ontology.
claims.source_quote: It concludes by defining law as structured being-with, a term that encapsulates its relational ontology.
claims.note: The author asserts a definition of law as a kind of entity with a relational ontological structure.

claims.claim: Legal entities are continuants dependent on recognition.
claims.source_quote: a realist ontology that treats legal entities as continuants dependent on recognition.
claims.note: Asserts the kind (continuants) and a dependency relation for legal entities.

claims.claim: Obligations are specifically dependent continuants that emerge from acts of recognition between agents.
claims.source_quote: It defines obligations as specifically dependent continuants that emerge from acts of recognition between agents and persist until realized or nullified.
claims.note: Asserts the kind (specifically dependent continuants) and the origin relation for obligations.

claims.claim: Obligations persist until they are realized or nullified.
claims.source_quote: obligations as specifically dependent continuants that emerge from acts of recognition between agents and persist until realized or nullified.
claims.note: Asserts a temporal/dispositional property of obligations.

claims.claim: Recognition is the ontological act that animates law, transforming ephemeral social gestures into enduring structures.
claims.source_quote: Recognition is described as the ontological act that animates law, turning ephemeral social gestures into enduring structures.
claims.note: Asserts a role/function of recognition in producing enduring legal structures.

claims.claim: Courts, legislatures, and other institutional bodies are repair nodes that stabilize relational fields.
claims.source_quote: treating courts, legislatures, and other bodies as repair nodes that stabilize relational fields.
claims.note: Asserts a functional role for institutional bodies as a kind of entity (repair nodes) with a stabilizing function.

claims.claim: Law operates through role-bearing individuals whose actions instantiate institutional functions.
claims.source_quote: Chapter Six, Legal Roles and Social Participation demonstrates how law operates through role-bearing individuals whose actions instantiate institutional functions.
claims.note: Asserts a relational structure between individuals, roles, and institutions constitutive of law.

claims.claim: Status functions are dependent continuants that arise from institutional processes.
claims.source_quote: how status functions, Searle's notion that 'X counts as Y in context C', can be modeled ontologically as dependent continuants that arise from institutional processes.
claims.note: Author endorses modeling status functions as a subkind (dependent continuants) arising from institutional processes.

claims.claim: Property rights are relational continuants maintained by legal recognition.
claims.source_quote: showing how property rights are realized as relational continuants maintained by legal recognition.
claims.note: Asserts the kind (relational continuants) and maintenance relation for property rights.

claims.claim: Trials, testimony, and artifacts function as processes that produce and sustain juridical truth.
claims.source_quote: mapping how trials, testimony, and artifacts function as processes that produce and sustain juridical truth.
claims.note: Asserts a functional role for these entities as processes producing juridical truth.

claims.claim: Every legal judgment or transaction modifies the structure of legal reality.
claims.source_quote: revealing how every judgment or transaction modifies the structure of legal reality.
claims.note: Asserts a causal/relational property: judgments and transactions bear a modification relation to legal reality.

claims.claim: Contradiction debt is the accumulation of unresolved conflicts within a legal system.
claims.source_quote: the concept of contradiction debt is introduced to describe the accumulation of unresolved conflicts within a legal system.
claims.note: Introduces and defines contradiction debt as a kind of entity with a specific character.

claims.claim: Justice is the restoration of structural coherence within the architecture of recognition.
claims.source_quote: Justice is defined not as abstract fairness but as the restoration of structural coherence within the architecture of recognition.
claims.note: Author positively defines justice in ontological terms as a restorative process.

claims.claim: Computational systems can participate in legal reasoning if they instantiate legitimate roles within recognized institutions.
claims.source_quote: computational systems can represent, and even participate in, legal reasoning, provided they instantiate legitimate roles within recognized institutions.
claims.note: Asserts a conditional existential claim about computational systems bearing legal roles.

claims.claim: Justice is not an external ideal imposed upon law but the internal measure of its coherence.
claims.source_quote: It argues that justice is not an external ideal imposed upon law but the internal measure of its coherence.
claims.note: Author positively asserts the ontological status of justice relative to law.

claims.claim: A just law or institution maintains the integrity of recognition and obligation within its structure.
claims.source_quote: To say that a law or institution is just is to say that it maintains the integrity of recognition and obligation within its structure.
claims.note: Defines justice as a structural property of laws and institutions involving recognition and obligation.

claims.claim: Persons, institutions, and obligations co-constitute the social world through a network of relations.
claims.source_quote: the network of relations through which persons, institutions, and obligations co-constitute the social world.
claims.note: Asserts a relational ontology in which these kinds jointly constitute the social world.

claims.claim: Law is an ontological structure that stabilizes human coexistence through recognition, obligation, and repair.
claims.source_quote: law is an ontological structure that stabilizes human coexistence through recognition, obligation, and repair.
claims.note: Central thesis: asserts law's kind (ontological structure) and its function/relation to human coexistence.

claims.claim: Law endures because it is built to be mended.
claims.source_quote: It endures because it is built to be mended.
claims.note: Asserts a dispositional property of law: its persistence is grounded in its capacity for repair.

claims.claim: Law is an architecture of social being rather than a linguistic or moral construct.
claims.source_quote: By treating law as an architecture of social being rather than as a linguistic or moral construct
claims.note: Author positively asserts law's ontological kind, distinguishing it from linguistic or moral constructs.

claims.claim: The diagrams in the book express ontological relations between agents, roles, institutions, and obligations.
claims.source_quote: every diagram expresses an ontological relation, between agents and roles, roles and institutions, obligations and their bearers, without reducing them to metaphor.
claims.note: Asserts that specific ontological relations obtain between these kinds of entities.

claims.claim: Legal relations exist within a framework of being-with that allows justice to take form.
claims.source_quote: the enduring framework of being-with that allows justice to take form in the world.
claims.note: Asserts the existence of an enduring relational framework (being-with) as the ground of justice.

claims.claim: Procedures are the mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities.
claims.source_quote: They are the mechanisms by which potentialities become actualities, turning the abstract conditions of recognition into concrete instances of legal facticity.
claims.note: Direct assertion about the ontological role and function of procedures.

claims.claim: Procedural realization of facts is the bridge between law's dynamic and static dimensions.
claims.source_quote: The procedural realization of facts is thus the bridge between law's dynamic and static dimensions, between the lived temporality of adjudication and the enduring reality of institutional record.
claims.note: Author asserts a relational property of procedural realization connecting two dimensions of law.

claims.claim: Every legal system relies on procedures because law's ontology demands them.
claims.source_quote: Every legal system relies on procedures because law's ontology demands them.
claims.note: Plain assertion about a property of every legal system and a requirement grounded in law's ontology.

claims.claim: Recognition alone is insufficient to create durable legal entities.
claims.source_quote: Recognition alone is insufficient to create durable entities; it must be expressed, recorded, and stabilized through processes that distribute acknowledgment across agents and time.
claims.note: Asserts a property of recognition: it is insufficient by itself for creating durable entities.

claims.claim: Procedures are the means by which recognition is operationalized.
claims.source_quote: These processes are not mere administrative formalities; they are the means by which recognition is operationalized.
claims.note: Asserts a functional/relational role of procedural processes with respect to recognition.

claims.claim: Without procedures, legal facts would remain fleeting intentions rather than enduring components of the legal world.
claims.source_quote: In their absence, legal facts would remain fleeting intentions rather than enduring components of the legal world.
claims.note: Asserts a counterfactual ontological property: legal facts require procedures for enduring existence.

claims.claim: A verdict, judgment, or deed achieves its ontological status only through a procedural framework.
claims.source_quote: A verdict, a judgment, or a deed achieves its ontological status only when it is processed through a procedural framework that integrates it into the system's memory.
claims.note: Asserts a dependency relation: ontological status of legal acts depends on procedural framework.

claims.claim: Procedure is the temporal realization of law's structural being.
claims.source_quote: Thus, procedure is not ancillary to substance; it is the temporal realization of law's structural being.
claims.note: Asserts a fundamental ontological identity/role for procedure.

claims.claim: Procedural realization of facts involves the realization of dependent continuants through occurrents.
claims.source_quote: In ontological terms, the procedural realization of facts involves two primary relations: the realization of dependent continuants (functions, obligations, roles) through occurrents...
claims.note: Direct ontological claim about a primary relation in procedural realization.

claims.claim: Procedural realization of facts involves the creation of new dependent continuants that persist after the process concludes.
claims.source_quote: ...and the creation of new dependent continuants (records, rights, decisions) that persist after the process concludes.
claims.note: Asserts the existence and persistence of new dependent continuants created through procedure.

claims.claim: A trial is an occurrent that realizes the function of adjudication inherent in the judicial institution.
claims.source_quote: A trial, for example, realizes the function of adjudication inherent in the judicial institution. It is an occurrent that brings into being new continuants, judgments, findings, sentences.
claims.note: Asserts that trials are occurrents bearing a realization relation to the function of adjudication.

claims.claim: Judgments, findings, and sentences are continuants that endure as parts of the legal system.
claims.source_quote: It is an occurrent that brings into being new continuants, judgments, findings, sentences, that endure as parts of the legal system.
claims.note: Asserts that judgments, findings, and sentences are a kind (continuants) and are parts of the legal system.

claims.claim: The act of filing a petition creates a new legal continuant: the case file.
claims.source_quote: ...the act of filing a petition realizes the role-based function of initiating adjudication and creates a new legal continuant: the case file, an informational artifact that embodies the existence of a dispute within the institutional structure.
claims.note: Asserts existence of a new continuant (case file) created by filing and its status as an informational artifact.

claims.claim: The case file is an informational artifact that embodies the existence of a dispute within the institutional structure.
claims.source_quote: ...the case file, an informational artifact that embodies the existence of a dispute within the institutional structure.
claims.note: Asserts a kind membership and a property/relation of the case file.

claims.claim: A trial is a complex occurrent that realizes multiple functions while producing enduring entities.
claims.source_quote: The trial, in its entirety, is thus a complex occurrent that realizes multiple functions while producing enduring entities.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership (complex occurrent) and functional/generative properties of trials.

claims.claim: The submission of evidence transforms physical artifacts or testimony into recognized evidential entities.
claims.source_quote: The submission of evidence transforms physical artifacts or testimony into recognized evidential entities, dependent continuants that exist only within the trial's field of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a transformation relation producing dependent continuants from physical artifacts.

claims.claim: Evidential entities are dependent continuants that exist only within the trial's field of recognition.
claims.source_quote: ...recognized evidential entities, dependent continuants that exist only within the trial's field of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership and an existence condition for evidential entities.

claims.claim: The final judgment is a generative event that brings into being new legal facts.
claims.source_quote: The final judgment is not merely a conclusion; it is a generative event that brings into being new legal facts, rights affirmed, obligations imposed, statuses changed.
claims.note: Asserts that the judgment is an event with a generative ontological role.

claims.claim: Once rendered, a judgment becomes a continuant that persists as precedent, record, and enforceable norm.
claims.source_quote: Once rendered, the judgment becomes a continuant that persists through the institutional system as precedent, record, and enforceable norm.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership (continuant) and persistence properties of rendered judgments.

claims.claim: The trial's purpose is ontological as much as epistemic.
claims.source_quote: From this perspective, the trial's purpose is ontological as much as epistemic.
claims.note: Asserts a property (dual purpose) of the trial.

claims.claim: The trial creates legal facts through regulated processes of recognition and validation.
claims.source_quote: It does not simply discover facts but creates legal facts through regulated processes of recognition and validation.
claims.note: Asserts that trials have a creative ontological function with respect to legal facts.

claims.claim: Factual truth pertains to correspondence with the brute world, while legal truth pertains to coherence within the network of recognition.
claims.source_quote: The distinction between factual truth and legal truth is therefore structural: factual truth pertains to correspondence with the brute world, while legal truth pertains to coherence within the network of recognition produced by procedural realization.
claims.note: Asserts structural difference between two kinds of truth and their respective ontological grounds.

claims.claim: A verdict that contradicts empirical reality can still constitute a valid legal fact if it satisfies procedural and institutional dependencies.
claims.source_quote: A verdict that contradicts empirical reality can still constitute a valid legal fact if it satisfies procedural and institutional dependencies.
claims.note: Asserts a sufficient condition for legal facthood, committing to the ontological autonomy of legal facts.

claims.claim: Legal facts operate on a level of dependence defined by procedures rather than physical causality.
claims.source_quote: Legal facts do not compete with natural facts; they operate on a different level of dependence, one defined by procedures rather than physical causality.
claims.note: Asserts that legal facts have a distinct ontological level and dependence structure.

claims.claim: The act of filing transforms an intention or claim into an institutional entity by embedding it in a system of record.
claims.source_quote: The act of filing transforms an intention or claim into an institutional entity by embedding it in a system of record.
claims.note: Asserts a transformation relation through which institutional entities come into existence.

claims.claim: The case entry is a continuant that becomes part of the court's institutional ontology and persists even if the complaint is dismissed.
claims.source_quote: ...jointly create a new continuant, the case entry, which becomes part of the court's institutional ontology. This entity persists even if the complaint is later dismissed or withdrawn.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership, part-of relation, and persistence property of the case entry.

claims.claim: The case file is an information artifact that is the vessel through which recognition achieves material endurance.
claims.source_quote: The case file, as an information artifact, is the vessel through which recognition achieves material endurance.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership and functional role of the case file.

claims.claim: Each subsequent filing modifies the structure of the case file, updating the ontology of the dispute.
claims.source_quote: Each subsequent filing modifies the structure of this artifact, updating the ontology of the dispute.
claims.note: Asserts a modification relation between filings and the ontological structure of the dispute.

claims.claim: Filing is both a procedural occurrent and a means of extending law's temporal continuity.
claims.source_quote: In this way, filing is both a procedural occurrent and a means of extending law's temporal continuity.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership (procedural occurrent) and a functional property of filing.

claims.claim: Information artifacts are the physical or digital substrates that carry dependent continuants and materialize institutional recognition.
claims.source_quote: They are the physical or digital substrates that carry dependent continuants, texts, signatures, seals, data entries, that materialize institutional recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a property and relational role of information artifacts within legal ontology.

claims.claim: Within BFO, information artifacts are independent continuants bearing information content entities (ICEs).
claims.source_quote: Within BFO, these artifacts are independent continuants bearing information content entities (ICEs).
claims.note: Asserts kind membership and a bearing relation for information artifacts within BFO ontology.

claims.claim: An ICE is a generically dependent continuant that can exist on multiple bearers.
claims.source_quote: An ICE is a generically dependent continuant that can exist on multiple bearers, such as the same statute stored in different media, but whose content is defined by a particular structure of symbols and meanings.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership and a property of ICEs.

claims.claim: In law, ICEs include statutes, contracts, verdicts, and records.
claims.source_quote: In law, ICEs include statutes, contracts, verdicts, and records.
claims.note: Asserts subkind/membership relations: statutes, contracts, verdicts, records are ICEs.

claims.claim: ICEs are the vehicles of legal facticity: they externalize, preserve, and transmit recognition.
claims.source_quote: They are the vehicles of legal facticity: the means by which recognition is externalized, preserved, and transmitted.
claims.note: Asserts a functional role of ICEs in the ontology of legal facts.

claims.claim: Without information artifacts, the network of recognition could not persist beyond individual acts.
claims.source_quote: Without them, the network of recognition could not persist beyond the temporal boundaries of individual acts.
claims.note: Asserts a necessary condition for the persistence of the recognition network.

claims.claim: A procedural act (trial, filing, enactment) is an occurrent through which a legal fact is created.
claims.source_quote: Occurrent: The procedural act (trial, filing, enactment) through which a fact is created.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership (occurrent) and a generative role for procedural acts.

claims.claim: The legal relation or status generated by procedure (right, obligation, decision) is a dependent continuant.
claims.source_quote: Dependent Continuant: The legal relation or status generated (right, obligation, decision).
claims.note: Asserts kind membership of rights, obligations, and decisions as dependent continuants.

claims.claim: The information artifact is the material or digital bearer that embodies the dependent continuant.
claims.source_quote: Information Artifact: The material or digital bearer that embodies the dependent continuant.
claims.note: Asserts a bearing/embodiment relation between information artifacts and dependent continuants.

claims.claim: The institutional continuant (court, registry, agency) is the system that maintains recognition of the artifact.
claims.source_quote: Institutional Continuant: The system (court, registry, agency) that maintains recognition of the artifact.
claims.note: Asserts kind membership and a functional property of institutional continuants.

claims.claim: Law is an architecture of social being.
claims.source_quote: By treating law as an architecture of social being rather than as a linguistic or moral construct, we can understand both its necessity and its fragility.
claims.note: The author endorses this characterization of law as a positive ontological claim about what law is, contrasting it with alternatives.

claims.claim: Law has an enduring framework of being-with that allows justice to take form in the world.
claims.source_quote: the enduring framework of being-with that allows justice to take form in the world.
claims.note: The author asserts the existence of this framework as a structural feature of law that sustains it.

claims.claim: Law endures because it is built to be mended.
