claims.claim: Open-source software, creative commons licensing, and public data repositories are forms of collective ownership realized through distributed recognition.
claims.source_quote: Open-source software, creative commons licensing, and public data repositories are contemporary expressions of collective ownership realized through distributed recognition.
claims.note: Asserts that these entities are instances of collective ownership with distributed recognition.

claims.claim: An open-source license is an information artifact encoding conditions of recognition.
claims.source_quote: The open-source license, for example, functions as an information artifact encoding the conditions of recognition: it specifies who may use, modify, and distribute the software.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological kind (information artifact) and function of an open-source license.

claims.claim: In digital commons, the network of recognition among users and contributors sustains the property relation.
claims.source_quote: The network of recognition among users and contributors sustains the property relation.
claims.note: Asserts a sustaining dependency relation between a recognition network and the property relation.

claims.claim: In digital commons, recognition is mediated by digital infrastructure rather than centralized authority.
claims.source_quote: The commons is not merely public but networked: recognition is mediated by digital infrastructure rather than centralized authority.
claims.note: Asserts a relational/mediation property distinguishing digital commons from other forms.

claims.claim: The tragedy of the commons is a breakdown of collective recognition.
claims.source_quote: The so-called 'tragedy of the commons' is, in ontological terms, a breakdown of collective recognition: when individual actions cease to align with the shared dependencies that define common ownership, the property relation disintegrates.
claims.note: Asserts what the tragedy of the commons is ontologically—a kind of recognition failure.

claims.claim: When individual actions cease to align with shared dependencies of common ownership, the property relation disintegrates.
claims.source_quote: When individual actions cease to align with the shared dependencies that define common ownership, the property relation disintegrates.
claims.note: Asserts a causal/conditional ontological claim about property relation dissolution.

claims.claim: Successful commons management depends on the resilience of its recognition network.
claims.source_quote: Successful commons management, whether ecological or digital, depends on the resilience of its recognition network, the capacity of its institutions to maintain coherence among distributed bearers.
claims.note: Asserts a dependency relation between commons success and recognition network resilience.

claims.claim: In private property, the owner-object-institution relation is individualized and exclusive.
claims.source_quote: In private property, the relation is individualized and exclusive; in the commons, it is collective and inclusive.
claims.note: Asserts properties of the triadic relation in the case of private property.

claims.claim: In the commons, the owner-object-institution relation is collective and inclusive.
claims.source_quote: In private property, the relation is individualized and exclusive; in the commons, it is collective and inclusive.
claims.note: Asserts properties of the triadic relation in the case of the commons.

claims.claim: Law's reality is relational, not material.
claims.source_quote: Both forms demonstrate that law's reality is not material but relational: the world of ownership, whether private or public, exists only insofar as recognition persists.
claims.note: Direct ontological assertion about the nature of law's reality.

claims.claim: The world of ownership exists only insofar as recognition persists.
claims.source_quote: The world of ownership, whether private or public, exists only insofar as recognition persists.
claims.note: Asserts an existence condition for ownership on recognition.

claims.claim: Pluralist systems tolerate overlapping norms, jurisdictions, and values.
claims.source_quote: Pluralist systems, those that tolerate overlapping norms, jurisdictions, and values, necessarily generate more contradiction but also possess greater repair capacity.
claims.note: Asserts a defining property of pluralist systems.

claims.claim: Pluralist systems necessarily generate more contradiction than non-pluralist systems.
claims.source_quote: Pluralist systems, those that tolerate overlapping norms, jurisdictions, and values, necessarily generate more contradiction but also possess greater repair capacity.
claims.note: Asserts a causal/structural property of pluralist systems.

claims.claim: Pluralist systems possess greater repair capacity than authoritarian systems.
claims.source_quote: Pluralist systems, those that tolerate overlapping norms, jurisdictions, and values, necessarily generate more contradiction but also possess greater repair capacity.
claims.note: Asserts a comparative dispositional property of pluralist systems.

claims.claim: Authoritarian systems minimize contradiction by suppressing alternative recognitions.
claims.source_quote: Authoritarian systems, by contrast, minimize contradiction by suppressing alternative recognitions, but at the cost of rigidity and fragility.
claims.note: Asserts a property and mechanism of authoritarian systems.

claims.claim: Authoritarian systems have the properties of rigidity and fragility.
claims.source_quote: Authoritarian systems, by contrast, minimize contradiction by suppressing alternative recognitions, but at the cost of rigidity and fragility.
claims.note: Asserts dispositional properties of authoritarian systems.

claims.claim: Contradiction debt in authoritarian systems tends to culminate in collapse.
claims.source_quote: When contradiction debt arises in such systems, it cannot be easily dissipated through institutional repair and instead tends to culminate in collapse.
claims.note: Asserts a causal/structural disposition of contradiction debt in authoritarian systems.

claims.claim: Pluralism is a condition of ontological resilience in sustainable legal systems.
claims.source_quote: pluralism is not a political preference but a condition of ontological resilience in sustainable legal systems.
claims.note: The author explicitly advances this as an ontological claim in his own voice, asserting the role/function of pluralism.

claims.claim: Systems capable of integrating and repairing contradiction maintain coherence over time.
claims.source_quote: Systems capable of integrating and repairing contradiction maintain coherence over time; those that cannot, disintegrate.
claims.note: Asserts a property/disposition of contradiction-repairing systems.

claims.claim: Systems incapable of integrating and repairing contradiction disintegrate.
claims.source_quote: Systems capable of integrating and repairing contradiction maintain coherence over time; those that cannot, disintegrate.
claims.note: Asserts a dispositional outcome for systems lacking repair capacity.

claims.claim: Evidence belongs to the class of information-bearing dependent continuants.
claims.source_quote: evidence belongs to the class of information-bearing dependent continuants, entities that exist only through recognition and serve as mediators between brute occurrences and institutional judgment.
claims.note: Direct ontological classification of evidence as a kind of entity.

claims.claim: Information-bearing dependent continuants exist only through recognition.
claims.source_quote: evidence belongs to the class of information-bearing dependent continuants, entities that exist only through recognition and serve as mediators between brute occurrences and institutional judgment.
claims.note: Asserts a property of the class of entities to which evidence belongs.

claims.claim: Information-bearing dependent continuants serve as mediators between brute occurrences and institutional judgment.
claims.source_quote: entities that exist only through recognition and serve as mediators between brute occurrences and institutional judgment.
claims.note: Asserts a functional/relational role of information-bearing dependent continuants.

claims.claim: Evidence is made through processes of recognition and contextualization, not simply found in the world.
claims.source_quote: Evidence, unlike raw data, is not simply found in the world; it is made through processes of recognition and contextualization.
claims.note: Asserts a property and origin of evidence as an entity.

claims.claim: A fingerprint, video recording, or witness statement becomes evidence only when a legal institution interprets and integrates it within juridical relevance.
claims.source_quote: A fingerprint, a video recording, or a witness's statement becomes evidence only when a legal institution interprets and integrates it within the field of juridical relevance.
claims.note: Asserts a condition for the existence of evidence as evidence—an ontological dependency claim.

claims.claim: The act of institutional interpretation is an occurrent of recognition.
claims.source_quote: It is this act of interpretation, an occurrent of recognition, that transforms a physical or informational entity into a bearer of evidential force.
claims.note: Classifies the act of interpretation as a specific kind of entity (occurrent).

claims.claim: Evidence is a recognized information artifact.
claims.source_quote: evidence is a recognized information artifact: a material or digital continuant carrying content that has been conferred a specific epistemic function within law's framework.
claims.note: Direct ontological classification of evidence.

claims.claim: Evidence is a material or digital continuant carrying content.
claims.source_quote: a material or digital continuant carrying content that has been conferred a specific epistemic function within law's framework.
claims.note: Asserts the categorical type and properties of evidence.

claims.claim: Evidence has been conferred a specific epistemic function within law's framework.
claims.source_quote: a material or digital continuant carrying content that has been conferred a specific epistemic function within law's framework.
claims.note: Asserts a functional property of evidence.

claims.claim: Data are information content entities that exist independently of their use or recognition.
claims.source_quote: Data are information content entities that exist independently of their use or recognition. They are mere representations or traces of events, measurements, recordings, or stored signals, whose significance is not yet defined.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological kind and property of data.

claims.claim: Testimony is a speech act occurrent—a process through which an agent conveys information.
claims.source_quote: Testimony, by contrast, is a speech act occurrent: a process through which an agent conveys information, intending recognition by others.
claims.note: Classifies testimony as a specific kind of entity (occurrent/process).

claims.claim: Testimony is transient, realized in time through performance.
claims.source_quote: Testimony may generate data (as in transcripts or recordings) but is itself transient, realized in time through performance.
claims.note: Asserts a property of testimony as an entity.

claims.claim: Evidence arises when data or testimony are recognized as relevant to a legal issue and incorporated into an institutional process.
claims.source_quote: Evidence, finally, arises when data or testimony are recognized as relevant to a legal issue and incorporated into an institutional process.
claims.note: Asserts the conditions and relational structure for evidence's existence.

claims.claim: Evidence is data with juridical status.
claims.source_quote: Evidence, in this sense, is data with juridical status: it bears a specific dependent continuant, evidential weight, that exists only within the system of recognition defined by procedural rules and institutional authority.
claims.note: Asserts a subkind or categorical relationship between evidence and data.

claims.claim: Evidential weight is a dependent continuant that exists only within the system of recognition defined by procedural rules and institutional authority.
claims.source_quote: it bears a specific dependent continuant, evidential weight, that exists only within the system of recognition defined by procedural rules and institutional authority.
claims.note: Classifies evidential weight as a dependent continuant and asserts its dependency relation.

claims.claim: Proof is not an entity but a state of institutional coherence.
claims.source_quote: It is not an entity but a state of institutional coherence achieved when recognized evidence satisfies the criteria of persuasion set by the system.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological status (or non-status as a discrete entity) of proof.

claims.claim: Proof is an emergent configuration within the field of recognition.
claims.source_quote: Proof, therefore, is not an additional artifact but an emergent configuration within the field of recognition, a condition in which evidential dependencies align to produce a coherent judgment.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological character of proof as an emergent configuration.

claims.claim: Evidence denotes the recognized relation between information and event.
claims.source_quote: the former denotes the recognized relation between information and event, while the latter denotes the achieved coherence among such relations within an adjudicative context.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property defining evidence ontologically.

claims.claim: Proof denotes the achieved coherence among evidential relations within an adjudicative context.
claims.source_quote: the latter denotes the achieved coherence among such relations within an adjudicative context.
claims.note: Asserts the relational/structural nature of proof.

claims.claim: In law, evidence ceases to exist the moment recognition is withdrawn.
claims.source_quote: in law, evidence ceases to exist the moment recognition is withdrawn.
claims.note: Asserts an existential dependency of evidence on institutional recognition.

claims.claim: The ontology of evidence is inseparable from the institutional structures that confer and maintain its meaning.
claims.source_quote: This dependence on recognition means that the ontology of evidence is inseparable from the institutional structures that confer and maintain its meaning.
claims.note: Asserts a constitutive dependency relation between evidence and institutional structures.

claims.claim: Evidence is a dependent continuant that inheres in an information artifact.
claims.source_quote: Evidence is a dependent continuant that: Inheres in an information artifact (a physical or digital bearer, such as a document, photograph, or recording).
claims.note: Asserts the ontological type of evidence and its inherence relation to an information artifact.

claims.claim: Evidence depends on an institutional continuant for its existence as evidence.
claims.source_quote: Depends on an institutional continuant (a court, tribunal, or agency) for its existence as evidence.
claims.note: Asserts a dependency relation between evidence and institutional continuants.

claims.claim: Evidence is realized through procedural occurrents such as investigation, submission, and evaluation.
claims.source_quote: Is realized through procedural occurrents (investigation, submission, and evaluation).
claims.note: Asserts a realization relation between evidence and procedural occurrents.

claims.claim: Evidence gains persistence through record artifacts that embody institutional recognition.
claims.source_quote: Gains persistence through record artifacts (transcripts, exhibits, databases) that embody institutional recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property: evidence's persistence depends on record artifacts.

claims.claim: Pluralism is a condition of ontological resilience in sustainable legal systems.
claims.source_quote: pluralism is not a political preference but a condition of ontological resilience in sustainable legal systems.
claims.note: Author explicitly asserts this as an ontological claim advanced throughout the work.

claims.claim: Legal systems capable of integrating and repairing contradiction maintain coherence over time.
claims.source_quote: Systems capable of integrating and repairing contradiction maintain coherence over time; those that cannot, disintegrate.
claims.note: Direct assertion about a property of legal systems as a kind of entity.

claims.claim: Every unfulfilled obligation or unresolved injustice is a residue of incoherence within the structure of recognition.
claims.source_quote: Every unfulfilled obligation or unresolved injustice represents a residue of incoherence within the structure of recognition, a moral tension awaiting repair.
claims.note: Author asserts a property/relation of unfulfilled obligations and unresolved injustices within legal ontology.

claims.claim: Transitional justice, reparations, and truth commissions are large-scale repair mechanisms for legal ontology.
claims.source_quote: Transitional justice, reparations, and truth commissions all function as large-scale repair mechanisms, designed to reconcile past contradictions between law and moral recognition.
claims.note: Author asserts a functional role for these entities within legal ontology.

claims.claim: Transitional justice mechanisms retroactively redefine which legal entities continue to exist as valid.
claims.source_quote: They operate by retroactively redefining which entities, verdicts, laws, or acts, continue to exist as valid within the reconstructed ontology of justice.
claims.note: Asserts a relational and existential property of transitional justice mechanisms.

claims.claim: The annulment of unjust laws extinguishes incoherent continuants, restoring integrity to the legal system's being.
claims.source_quote: The annulment of unjust laws or the posthumous exoneration of the wrongly convicted exemplify this process: the legal system repairs its own history by extinguishing incoherent continuants, thereby restoring integrity to its being.
claims.note: Author asserts an ontological function of legal annulment as extinguishing continuants.

claims.claim: Justice is the ongoing equilibrium between contradiction and repair.
claims.source_quote: In this view, justice itself can be defined as the ongoing equilibrium between contradiction and repair.
claims.note: Author advances a definitional/ontological claim about the nature of justice.

claims.claim: A just system is one that can transform conflict into coherence through structured recognition.
claims.source_quote: A just system is not one without conflict but one that can transform conflict into coherence through structured recognition.
claims.note: Author asserts a property that defines the kind 'just system'.

claims.claim: Contradiction debt becomes destructive only when repair ceases.
claims.source_quote: Contradiction is inevitable, but debt is manageable; it becomes destructive only when repair ceases.
claims.note: Author asserts a causal/dispositional property of contradiction debt.

claims.claim: Law's ontological vocation includes preserving recognition by absorbing and resolving contradiction debt.
claims.source_quote: A vital part of law's ontological vocation, therefore, is to preserve the world of recognition by absorbing and resolving contradiction debt through procedural and institutional means.
claims.note: Author asserts a functional role/vocation of law as a kind of entity.

claims.claim: Each act of interpretation, judgment, or reform contributes to the continuous ontological maintenance of law.
claims.source_quote: Each act of interpretation, judgment, or reform contributes to this continuous ontological maintenance, a process by which law not only orders society but perpetually reconstructs the very conditions of its existence.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property linking legal acts to ontological maintenance.

claims.claim: Contradiction is an inevitable feature of law's relational ontology, not a defect in its design.
claims.source_quote: Contradiction, as established in the preceding section, is not a defect in law's design but an inevitable feature of its relational ontology.
claims.note: Author asserts an intrinsic property of law's ontological structure.

claims.claim: Law constitutes a network of dependent continuants.
claims.source_quote: they restore the integrity of the network of dependent continuants that constitutes law's being.
claims.note: Author asserts that law's being is constituted by a network of dependent continuants.

claims.claim: Every mechanism of legal correction is a form of ontological repair.
claims.source_quote: every mechanism of legal correction is a form of ontological repair, through which law reasserts its capacity to remain coherent despite constant tension and change.
claims.note: Author asserts a subkind/functional identity claim about legal correction mechanisms.

claims.claim: Repair mechanisms are occurrents that act upon continuants to restore coherence among their dependencies.
claims.source_quote: repair mechanisms can be modeled as occurrents, temporal processes that act upon existing continuants (laws, obligations, roles, or rights) to restore coherence among their dependencies.
claims.note: Author asserts the ontological category (occurrents) and function of repair mechanisms using BFO.

claims.claim: Repair mechanisms transform incoherent relations into coherent ones by altering the network of recognition.
claims.source_quote: they share the same ontological function: they transform incoherent relations into coherent ones by altering the network of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a shared functional property of all repair mechanisms.

claims.claim: Repair is the continuous realization of law's reflexivity as a system of interdependent continuants.
claims.source_quote: Repair, in this sense, is the continuous realization of law's reflexivity: its ability to recognize, critique, and reconstruct itself as a system of interdependent continuants.
claims.note: Author asserts an identity/property claim about repair in relation to law's reflexivity.

claims.claim: Adjudication is a localized repair process that identifies and resolves incompatible dependencies in a specific case.
claims.source_quote: Ontologically, adjudication functions as a localized repair process: an occurrent that identifies incompatible dependencies within a specific case and resolves them by privileging one recognition relation over another.
claims.note: Author asserts the ontological kind and function of adjudication.

claims.claim: Adjudication is an occurrent in the BFO sense.
claims.source_quote: Ontologically, adjudication functions as a localized repair process: an occurrent that identifies incompatible dependencies within a specific case.
claims.note: Author categorizes adjudication as an occurrent within BFO ontology.

claims.claim: The losing legal claim in adjudication continues to exist as a potential dependency in future recognition contexts.
claims.source_quote: The losing claim is not annihilated but subordinated, it continues to exist as a potential dependency in future recognition contexts.
claims.note: Author asserts a persistence property of subordinated legal claims.

claims.claim: Adjudication maintains coherence through controlled asymmetry without erasing diversity.
claims.source_quote: Through this selective preservation, adjudication repairs contradiction without erasing diversity. It exemplifies law's ability to maintain coherence through controlled asymmetry.
claims.note: Asserts a property and function of adjudication as a kind of legal process.

claims.claim: Amendment restructures the ontological architecture of recognition itself.
claims.source_quote: amendment restructures the ontological architecture of recognition itself.
claims.note: Author asserts a distinctive ontological function of legislative amendment.

claims.claim: Amendment alters the dependencies among institutional continuants such as statutes, constitutions, and regulatory bodies.
claims.source_quote: Legislative amendment alters the dependencies among institutional continuants, statutes, constitutions, and regulatory bodies, thereby recalibrating the parameters within which future contradictions will be managed.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property of amendment with respect to institutional continuants.

claims.claim: Amendment eliminates incoherent continuants and establishes new coherent dependencies aligned with current social recognition.
claims.source_quote: the institutional system modifies its recognition structures to eliminate incoherent continuants (invalid norms, unjust rules) and establish new, coherent dependencies aligned with current social recognition.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological operation performed by amendment on continuants.

claims.claim: Reinterpretation is a form of semantic repair that alters the meaning of existing dependent continuants without changing their formal identity.
claims.source_quote: Reinterpretation functions as semantic repair: it alters the meaning of existing dependent continuants without changing their formal identity.
claims.note: Author asserts the ontological category and distinctive property of reinterpretation.

claims.claim: Reinterpretation exemplifies continuant adaptation: persistence of a legal entity through internal modification of its dependent relations.
claims.source_quote: Ontologically, this process exemplifies continuant adaptation: the persistence of an entity (the law) through internal modification of its dependent relations.
claims.note: Author asserts an ontological pattern (continuant adaptation) instantiated by reinterpretation.

claims.claim: Transitional justice is the macro-ontological repair of entire systems of recognition.
claims.source_quote: Transitional justice is the macro-ontological repair of entire systems of recognition.
claims.note: Author asserts a definitional/ontological identity for transitional justice.

claims.claim: After periods of violence or repression, existing legal ontology is saturated with contradiction debt.
claims.source_quote: After periods of violence or repression, the existing legal ontology is saturated with contradiction debt: laws that sanctioned atrocities, verdicts grounded in coercion, and institutions complicit in moral collapse.
claims.note: Author asserts a property (saturation with contradiction debt) of post-repression legal ontologies.

claims.claim: Truth commissions, amnesties, reparations, and constitutional re-foundings are processes of ontological restoration.
claims.source_quote: Truth commissions, amnesties, reparations, and constitutional re-foundings all operate as processes of ontological restoration.
claims.note: Author asserts a functional/ontological role for these transitional justice mechanisms.

claims.claim: The apartheid legal system generated massive contradiction debt because its laws were internally coherent but externally incoherent with the moral ontology of justice.
claims.source_quote: The apartheid legal system generated massive contradiction debt: its laws were internally coherent but externally incoherent with the evolving global and moral ontology of justice.
claims.note: Author asserts a property of the apartheid legal system as an instance of contradiction debt generation.

claims.claim: The TRC reconstituted the field of recognition by acknowledging victims.
claims.source_quote: The TRC did not simply repeal those laws; it reconstituted the field of recognition by acknowledging victims.
claims.note: Author asserts an ontological operation performed by the TRC on the field of recognition.

claims.claim: The apartheid legal system generated massive contradiction debt.
claims.source_quote: The apartheid legal system generated massive contradiction debt: its laws were internally coherent but externally incoherent with the evolving global and moral ontology of justice.
claims.note: The author asserts a property ('contradiction debt') of the apartheid legal system as an ontological characterization.

claims.claim: The apartheid system's laws were internally coherent but externally incoherent with the moral ontology of justice.
claims.source_quote: its laws were internally coherent but externally incoherent with the evolving global and moral ontology of justice.
claims.note: The author asserts a relational property (incoherence with moral ontology) that the apartheid laws bore.

claims.claim: The TRC reconstituted the field of recognition by acknowledging victims, documenting truth, and redefining legitimacy.
claims.source_quote: The TRC did not simply repeal those laws; it reconstituted the field of recognition by acknowledging victims, documenting truth, and redefining legitimacy.
claims.note: The author asserts what the TRC did ontologically — it reconstituted a field (the field of recognition), which is an entity-level claim.

claims.claim: The TRC process created new dependent continuants: recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration.
claims.source_quote: This process created new dependent continuants, recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration, that replaced the invalid entities of prior law.
claims.note: The author asserts the existence of new entities (dependent continuants) brought into being by the TRC process.

claims.claim: Recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration are dependent continuants.
claims.source_quote: This process created new dependent continuants, recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration, that replaced the invalid entities of prior law.
claims.note: The author classifies recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration as belonging to the kind 'dependent continuant'.

claims.claim: The new dependent continuants replaced the invalid entities of prior law.
claims.source_quote: This process created new dependent continuants, recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration, that replaced the invalid entities of prior law.
claims.note: The author asserts a replacement relation between new entities and invalid prior legal entities.

claims.claim: The prior law's entities were invalid.
claims.source_quote: that replaced the invalid entities of prior law.
claims.note: The author attributes the property of invalidity to the entities generated by apartheid's prior law.

claims.claim: The result of the TRC process was the creation of a new coherence, not a return to a prior one.
claims.source_quote: The result was not a return to a preexisting coherence but the creation of a new one, more consistent with the moral and institutional conditions of the post-apartheid order.
claims.note: The author asserts that a new coherence (an entity with properties) was created, and characterizes its relation to prior states.

claims.claim: The new coherence is more consistent with the moral and institutional conditions of the post-apartheid order.
claims.source_quote: The result was not a return to a preexisting coherence but the creation of a new one, more consistent with the moral and institutional conditions of the post-apartheid order.
claims.note: The author asserts a relational property of the newly created coherence — its consistency with post-apartheid moral and institutional conditions.

claims.claim: Evidence depends on an institutional continuant (court, tribunal, or agency) for its existence.
claims.source_quote: Depends on an institutional continuant (a court, tribunal, or agency) for its existence as evidence.
claims.note: Direct assertion that evidence has an ontological dependency on institutional continuants.

claims.claim: Evidence is realized through procedural occurrents such as investigation, submission, and evaluation.
claims.source_quote: Is realized through procedural occurrents (investigation, submission, and evaluation).
claims.note: Asserts a realization relation between evidence and procedural occurrents.

claims.claim: Evidence gains persistence through record artifacts that embody institutional recognition.
claims.source_quote: Gains persistence through record artifacts (transcripts, exhibits, databases) that embody institutional recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a relation between evidence and record artifacts that sustains its continuity.

claims.claim: The material substrate of evidence carries informational content.
claims.source_quote: The material substrate carries informational content; institutional recognition confers relevance.
claims.note: Asserts a property (carrying informational content) of the material substrate layer.

claims.claim: Institutional recognition confers relevance on evidence.
claims.source_quote: institutional recognition confers relevance; procedural realization transforms relevance into juridical standing.
claims.note: Asserts that institutional recognition has the functional role of conferring relevance.

claims.claim: Procedural realization transforms evidential relevance into juridical standing.
claims.source_quote: procedural realization transforms relevance into juridical standing; and recording ensures continuity.
claims.note: Asserts a transformative relation between procedural realization and juridical standing.

claims.claim: An evidentiary system is a network of recognition processes and artifacts that collectively produce juridical truth.
claims.source_quote: the coherence of these layers constitutes what we call an evidentiary system, a network of recognition processes and artifacts that collectively produce juridical truth.
claims.note: Asserts what kind of entity an evidentiary system is and its function.

claims.claim: Evidence is inherently relational rather than substantial.
claims.source_quote: This framework also reveals why evidence is inherently relational rather than substantial.
claims.note: Direct ontological claim about the nature of evidence.

claims.claim: A blood sample has no evidential significance in itself.
claims.source_quote: A blood sample, for instance, has no evidential significance in itself.
claims.note: Asserts absence of an intrinsic property (evidential significance) in the object.

claims.claim: An object becomes evidence only when linked by recognized processes to an event and a person.
claims.source_quote: It becomes evidence only when linked by recognized processes like collection, labeling, testing, and authentication, to an event and a person.
claims.note: Asserts the relational conditions under which something becomes evidence.

claims.claim: If dependencies constituting the evidential relation are broken, an object ceases to exist as an evidential continuant.
claims.source_quote: If any of these dependencies are broken, such as a label misplaced, or a chain of custody violated, the evidential relation collapses. The object may remain physically intact, but its existence as an evidential continuant ceases.
claims.note: Asserts that evidential being depends on intact dependency relations.

claims.claim: Truth within legal systems depends on the integrity of recognition relations that sustain it.
claims.source_quote: truth within legal systems depends not merely on facts but on the integrity of recognition relations that sustain them.
claims.note: Asserts a dependency relation between legal truth and recognition relations.

claims.claim: Information artifacts are independent continuants bearing informational content.
claims.source_quote: As independent continuants bearing informational content, they provide the medium through which recognition persists over time.
claims.note: Asserts a kind and property of information artifacts.

claims.claim: Documents, exhibits, recordings, and digital files are the vehicles through which evidence exists as law.
claims.source_quote: Documents, exhibits, recordings, and digital files are not mere containers of evidence but the vehicles through which evidence exists as law.
claims.note: Asserts the functional/ontological role of these artifacts in sustaining evidence.

claims.claim: Information artifacts embody factual dependencies: structured representations encoding the link between occurrence and recognition.
claims.source_quote: They embody what might be called factual dependencies: structured representations that encode the link between occurrence and recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a property of information artifacts; slightly hedged by 'what might be called' but the author endorses the content.

claims.claim: A photograph introduced as evidence carries a dependent continuant of evidential force maintained by legal authenticity procedures.
claims.source_quote: it carries a dependent continuant of evidential force, maintained by the authenticity procedures of the legal system.
claims.note: Asserts that a photographic artifact has a dependent continuant as a property or part.

claims.claim: Once introduced into the legal record, an artifact becomes part of the enduring ontology of the case.
claims.source_quote: Once introduced into the record, such an artifact becomes part of the enduring ontology of the case: it exists as a legal entity long after the events it depicts have passed.
claims.note: Asserts that the artifact is a legal entity with persistence after its causal origin.

claims.claim: In contemporary systems, evidence increasingly exists as data stored in digital repositories.
claims.source_quote: In contemporary systems, evidence increasingly exists as data stored in digital repositories, where authenticity and chain of custody depend on metadata, timestamps, and cryptographic signatures.
claims.note: Asserts the kind/form evidence takes in contemporary digital systems.

claims.claim: Metadata, timestamps, and cryptographic signatures function as automated recognition processes.
claims.source_quote: These mechanisms function as automated recognition processes: algorithmic proxies for institutional verification.
claims.note: Asserts the functional role of these technical mechanisms.

claims.claim: A hash value or digital certificate acts as an institutional stand-in encoding recognition into the artifact itself.
claims.source_quote: A hash value or digital certificate, for instance, acts as an institutional stand-in, encoding recognition into the artifact itself.
claims.note: Asserts the role and function of hash values/certificates as institutional stand-ins.

claims.claim: Law and technology co-produce evidential being.
claims.source_quote: Law and technology co-produce evidential being, binding informational continuants to institutional authority through recursive validation.
claims.note: Asserts a co-productive causal/ontological relation between law and technology regarding evidence.

claims.claim: To declare something 'evidence' is to confer upon it ontological privilege as a bearer of potential truth within a public and coercive system.
claims.source_quote: To declare something 'evidence' is to confer upon it a specific kind of ontological privilege, it becomes a bearer of potential truth within a public and coercive system.
claims.note: Asserts that the act of recognition changes the ontological status and role of an entity.

claims.claim: The judge functions as arbiter of what enters as evidence and what is excluded.
claims.source_quote: The judge engages in this transformation as arbiter of what comes in as evidence and what is excluded. This is a vital role of the judge while serving as the trier of law.
claims.note: Asserts a role/function of the judge in evidential ontology.

claims.claim: Misrecognition produces ontological distortion: false facts institutionalized as truth.
claims.source_quote: Misrecognition at this level produces not merely epistemic error but ontological distortion, false facts institutionalized as truth.
claims.note: Asserts a property and effect of misrecognition at the ontological level.

claims.claim: In miscarriages of justice, recognition has conferred legitimacy upon entities that should not exist as evidence.
claims.source_quote: In miscarriages of justice, the failure is not that evidence is absent, but that recognition has gone awry, conferring legitimacy upon entities that should not exist as evidence at all.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological character of miscarriages of justice.

claims.claim: Evidence's being is processual: an ongoing interplay among data, institutions, and interpretation.
claims.source_quote: Its being is not static but processual: an ongoing interplay among data, institutions, and interpretation.
claims.note: Asserts a property (processual being) of evidence as an ontological entity.

claims.claim: The courtroom is a site where entities are created, validated, and sustained as building blocks of juridical reality.
claims.source_quote: The courtroom, in this view, is not a stage for the display of facts but a factory of ontology, where entities are created, validated, and sustained as the building blocks of juridical reality.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological function and role of the courtroom.

claims.claim: The trier of fact is an epistemic structure: a complex role-bearing configuration through which the legal system realizes the function of determining fact.
claims.source_quote: From an ontological perspective, the trier of fact is not merely a person or group but an epistemic structure: a complex role-bearing configuration through which the legal system realizes the function of determining fact.
claims.note: Asserts what kind of entity the trier of fact is.

claims.claim: The trier of fact's authority arises from institutional recognition of a specific role within a procedural context.
claims.source_quote: Its authority does not arise from individual cognition but from institutional recognition of a specific role within a procedural context.
claims.note: Asserts the source/ground of the trier of fact's authority.

claims.claim: The trier of fact is a role continuant realized in agents and sustained by institutions.
claims.source_quote: the trier of fact is a dependent continuant realized in agents and sustained by institutions. It is a role, not a substance.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological category and dependencies of the trier of fact.

claims.claim: The trier of fact is a role, not a substance.
claims.source_quote: It is a role, not a substance, a structured relation that exists only when borne by an individual or collective within a recognized legal process.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological kind of the trier of fact.

claims.claim: The trier of fact exists only when borne by an individual or collective within a recognized legal process.
claims.source_quote: a structured relation that exists only when borne by an individual or collective within a recognized legal process.
claims.note: Asserts the existential conditions of the role.

claims.claim: The trier of fact role is functionally dependent on institutional continuants and procedural occurrents.
claims.source_quote: This role is defined by its functional dependence on both institutional continuants (the court, tribunal, or administrative body) and procedural occurrents (the trial, hearing, or inquest).
claims.note: Asserts dependency relations defining the trier of fact role.

claims.claim: A verdict is a dependent continuant inhering in the institutional configuration that authorizes it.
claims.source_quote: A verdict is not merely a conclusion about events but a dependent continuant inhering in the institutional configuration that authorizes it.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological category and inherence relation of verdicts.

claims.claim: A verdict's being depends on the trier's recognized role within the institutional structure.
claims.source_quote: The verdict's being, therefore, depends on the trier's recognized role within this structure.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological dependency relation between verdict and the trier's role.

claims.claim: The jury's utterance occurs within a chain of recognition consisting of empanelment, instruction, deliberation, and court validation.
claims.source_quote: The jury's utterance occurs within a chain of recognition: empanelment, instruction, deliberation, and validation by the court.
claims.note: Asserts the structural composition of the jury's utterance as embedded in a chain of recognition—an ontological claim about relational structure.

claims.claim: Each stage of the chain realizes the dependencies that confer juridical status on the final judgment.
claims.source_quote: Each stage realizes the dependencies that confer juridical status on the final judgment.
claims.note: Asserts a realization relation between stages of legal process and the juridical status of the verdict.

claims.claim: The verdict's being depends on the trier's recognized role within the juridical structure.
claims.source_quote: The verdict's being, therefore, depends on the trier's recognized role within this structure.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological dependence relation between the verdict's existence and the trier's recognized role.

claims.claim: Without recognition, a verdict collapses into a mere utterance without legal existence.
claims.source_quote: Remove or corrupt that recognition, and the verdict collapses into a mere statement, a brute utterance without legal existence.
claims.note: Asserts that recognition is a necessary condition for a verdict's legal existence—an ontological claim about essential properties.

claims.claim: Epistemic authority in law has a hierarchical nature.
claims.source_quote: This dependency structure illustrates the hierarchical nature of epistemic authority in law.
claims.note: Asserts that epistemic authority in law is hierarchically structured—a property claim about a kind of entity.

claims.claim: The trier of fact's judgment is ontologically subordinate to the rule of recognition that defines the court's legitimacy.
claims.source_quote: The trier of fact's judgment is ontologically subordinate to the rule of recognition that defines the court's legitimacy.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological subordination relation between the trier's judgment and the rule of recognition.

claims.claim: The rule of recognition defines the court's legitimacy.
claims.source_quote: the rule of recognition that defines the court's legitimacy
claims.note: Asserts that the rule of recognition has the function/role of defining court legitimacy.

claims.claim: The trier of fact's judgment functions as the proximate source of factual truth within the legal system.
claims.source_quote: it functions as the proximate source of factual truth within the system.
claims.note: Asserts a functional role property of the trier's judgment within the legal system.

claims.claim: The South African transition created new dependent continuants: recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration.
claims.source_quote: This process created new dependent continuants, recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration, that replaced the invalid entities of prior law.
claims.note: Author asserts the existence of new dependent continuants as ontological entities created by the transitional process.

claims.claim: The South African transition replaced invalid legal entities with new ones.
claims.source_quote: This process created new dependent continuants, recognitions of harm, forgiveness, and restoration, that replaced the invalid entities of prior law.
claims.note: Author asserts that prior legal entities were invalid and were replaced, an ontological claim about the status and replacement of entities.

claims.claim: Systemic legal repair involves both destruction and creation of legal entities.
claims.source_quote: The South African experience demonstrates that repair at the systemic level involves both the destruction and creation of legal entities, a dual movement of ontological pruning and regeneration.
claims.note: Author asserts a property of systemic repair: it is a dual ontological movement of pruning and regeneration.

claims.claim: The Nuremberg and Tokyo Trials redefined the dependencies linking individuals, states, and international institutions.
claims.source_quote: By prosecuting crimes against humanity, these tribunals redefined the dependencies linking individuals, states, and international institutions.
claims.note: Author asserts that tribunals altered relational ontological dependencies among entities.

claims.claim: The Nuremberg and Tokyo Trials recognized individuals as subjects of international law.
claims.source_quote: They recognized new kinds of bearers (individuals as subjects of international law) and new dependent continuants (crimes that transcend jurisdictional boundaries).
claims.note: Author asserts that individuals are a new kind of bearer in international law—a subkind/entity-existence claim.

claims.claim: Crimes against humanity are dependent continuants that transcend jurisdictional boundaries.
claims.source_quote: They recognized new kinds of bearers (individuals as subjects of international law) and new dependent continuants (crimes that transcend jurisdictional boundaries).
claims.note: Author asserts that crimes transcending jurisdictions are a kind of dependent continuant—an ontological category claim.

claims.claim: Through resolving contradiction, law expands its own field of being.
claims.source_quote: It also demonstrated that repair can itself be generative: through resolving contradiction, law expands its own field of being.
claims.note: Author asserts a property/disposition of law: repair is generative and expands law's ontological domain.

claims.claim: Records, verdicts, and property relations derived from injustice persist as ontological residue of false recognition.
claims.source_quote: repair mechanisms must also address the ontological residue of false recognition, the persistence of records, verdicts, or property relations derived from injustice.
claims.note: Author asserts these entities persist and constitute ontological residue—an entity-existence and property claim.

claims.claim: Lustration, restitution, and legal nullification extinguish incoherent dependent continuants.
claims.source_quote: Mechanisms such as lustration (removal of compromised officials), restitution (return of confiscated property), and legal nullification (declaration of invalidity) serve to extinguish incoherent continuants that cannot be reconciled with the restored order.
claims.note: Author asserts a function/role of these mechanisms: they eliminate certain dependent continuants from existence.

claims.claim: Repair mechanisms perform ontological purification by formally withdrawing recognition.
claims.source_quote: These acts are not mere symbolic gestures; they perform the necessary work of ontological purification. By formally withdrawing recognition, the system eliminates entities whose continued existence would compromise coherence.
claims.note: Author asserts that withdrawing recognition eliminates entities—a claim about the ontological efficacy of legal acts.

claims.claim: Justice is a dynamic process of continuous repair rather than a static condition.
claims.source_quote: Justice, in this view, is not a static condition but a dynamic process of continuous repair, the perpetual balancing of contradiction debt through institutional evolution.
claims.note: Author asserts what justice is—an ontological characterization of justice as process.

claims.claim: Law is a living system that endures where repair persists.
claims.source_quote: Where repair persists, law endures as a living system; where repair fails, the world of law fractures into incoherence and decay.
claims.note: Author asserts that law has the property of being a living system, conditioned on repair—an ontological status claim.

claims.claim: Law is an organized structure of dependent continuants.
claims.source_quote: signals not merely a political or moral crisis but a metaphysical one: the disintegration of law's being as an organized structure of dependent continuants.
claims.note: Author asserts what law is ontologically: an organized structure of dependent continuants.

claims.claim: Law depends on the continuous and coherent functioning of recognition and repair.
claims.source_quote: legal systems reveal their true vulnerability, their dependence on the continuous and coherent functioning of recognition and repair.
claims.note: Author asserts a dependency relation: law's existence requires functioning recognition and repair.

claims.claim: In authoritarian systems, dependent continuants (rights, obligations, institutional roles) are forced into rigid hierarchies.
claims.source_quote: dependent continuants (rights, obligations, and institutional roles) are forced into rigid hierarchies that prevent adaptive repair.
claims.note: Author asserts a structural property of authoritarian legal entities—rigid hierarchical arrangement.

claims.claim: Authoritarianism represents a closed recognition field in which all entities derive existence from a single institutional node.
claims.source_quote: authoritarianism represents a closed recognition field. The institutional continuants that should mediate plural recognition... are subordinated to a single source of validation... all entities derive their existence from a single institutional node.
claims.note: Author asserts a structural ontological property of authoritarian law: monolithic, unidirectional recognition dependencies.

claims.claim: Law has an ontological requirement for distributed recognition.
claims.source_quote: This closure violates law's ontological requirement for distributed recognition, transforming what should be a network into a monolithic structure.
claims.note: Author asserts that distributed recognition is an ontological requirement of law—a necessary property claim.

claims.claim: In authoritarian systems, contradiction debt accumulates invisibly as latent incoherence.
claims.source_quote: Contradiction debt does not disappear; it becomes latent, internalized within a brittle order incapable of adjustment.
claims.note: Author asserts a property of contradiction debt in authoritarian systems: it becomes latent rather than disappearing.

claims.claim: Anomy is the state in which legal recognition persists in fragments but no longer constitutes a coherent world.
claims.source_quote: Ontologically, anomy is the state in which recognition persists in fragments but no longer constitutes a coherent world.
claims.note: Author asserts what anomy is ontologically—a definition with ontological content.

claims.claim: In anomic conditions, legal entities continue to be created but their dependencies are inconsistent or overlapping.
claims.source_quote: Legal entities continue to be created, but their dependencies are inconsistent or overlapping, producing systemic incoherence.
claims.note: Author asserts an ontological property of entities in anomic systems: inconsistent or overlapping dependencies.

claims.claim: Anomic collapse is a condition of contradiction saturation where every recognition conflicts with another.
claims.source_quote: The result is a condition of contradiction saturation, a state where every recognition conflicts with another, and no higher-order repair process remains to arbitrate.
claims.note: Author asserts what contradiction saturation is—an ontological state of the legal system.

claims.claim: In anomic decay, legal entities such as laws, offices, and procedures persist as historical artifacts lacking living recognition.
claims.source_quote: Their entities, laws, offices, procedures, persist as historical artifacts, lacking the living recognition necessary for their realization.
claims.note: Author asserts a property of entities in decayed systems: they persist nominally but lack the recognition required for ontological realization.

claims.claim: A state can exist only nominally while its ontology has already collapsed.
claims.source_quote: The state exists only nominally; its ontology has already collapsed.
claims.note: Author asserts that nominal existence and ontological existence can come apart—an entity-existence claim about states.

claims.claim: Each act of repair is an instance of law's reflexive ontology—its capacity to act upon itself as both object and subject of recognition.
claims.source_quote: Each act of repair is an instance of law's reflexive ontology, its capacity to act upon itself as both object and subject of recognition.
claims.note: Author asserts a property/disposition of law: reflexive ontology enabling self-directed recognition.

claims.claim: A state that exists only nominally has an ontology that has already collapsed.
claims.source_quote: he state exists only nominally; its ontology has already collapsed.
claims.note: Direct assertion about the ontological status of a nominally existing state.

claims.claim: In hybrid regimes or transitional societies, contradiction debt oscillates between rigidity and disintegration.
claims.source_quote: In hybrid regimes or transitional societies, contradiction debt oscillates between rigidity and disintegration.
claims.note: Asserts a property (oscillation between rigidity and disintegration) of contradiction debt in hybrid/transitional societies.

claims.claim: Partial repair processes allow the system to persist in chronic instability.
claims.source_quote: Partial repair processes, judicial independence without legislative reform, or free elections without institutional integrity, allow the system to persist but in chronic instability.
claims.note: Asserts a causal/dispositional property: partial repair processes produce chronic instability rather than resolution.

claims.claim: Law in hybrid or transitional contexts exists in a metastable state.
claims.source_quote: Law in these contexts exists in a metastable state: coherent enough to function but unable to resolve accumulated contradiction.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological property (metastability) of law in those contexts.

claims.claim: Metastable law is coherent enough to function but unable to resolve accumulated contradiction.
claims.source_quote: Law in these contexts exists in a metastable state: coherent enough to function but unable to resolve accumulated contradiction.
claims.note: Asserts two properties of metastable law: functional coherence and inability to resolve accumulated contradiction.

claims.claim: Ontologically precarious conditions depend on the constant exertion of compensatory effort.
claims.source_quote: These conditions are ontologically precarious, for they depend on the constant exertion of compensatory effort.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property: ontologically precarious conditions have compensatory effort as a necessary sustaining condition.

claims.claim: Hybrid or transitional conditions are ontologically precarious.
claims.source_quote: These conditions are ontologically precarious, for they depend on the constant exertion of compensatory effort.
claims.note: Direct assertion of an ontological property (precariousness) of these social/political conditions.

claims.claim: The trier of fact's judgment is ontologically subordinate to the rule of recognition.
claims.source_quote: The trier of fact's judgment is ontologically subordinate to the rule of recognition that defines the court's legitimacy, and yet it functions as the proximate source of factual truth within the system.
claims.note: Direct assertion of an ontological subordination relation between two entities.

claims.claim: The trier of fact's judgment is the proximate source of factual truth within the legal system.
claims.source_quote: The trier of fact's judgment is ontologically subordinate to the rule of recognition that defines the court's legitimacy, and yet it functions as the proximate source of factual truth within the system.
claims.note: Asserts a functional role/property of the trier's judgment.

claims.claim: The verdict is a secondary dependent continuant.
claims.source_quote: The verdict is a secondary dependent continuant: its existence depends on the sustained realization of multiple antecedent continuants, evidence, procedure, and institutional authority.
claims.note: Directly classifies the verdict as a kind of entity (secondary dependent continuant).

claims.claim: The verdict's existence depends on the sustained realization of evidence, procedure, and institutional authority.
claims.source_quote: The verdict is a secondary dependent continuant: its existence depends on the sustained realization of multiple antecedent continuants, evidence, procedure, and institutional authority.
claims.note: Asserts a dependence relation between the verdict and multiple antecedent continuants.

claims.claim: The verdict is a relational continuant linking the trier's role, the evidential record, and the institutional context.
claims.source_quote: In BFO terms, the verdict is a relational continuant linking the trier's role, the evidential record, and the institutional context.
claims.note: Asserts the verdict's ontological kind and its relational structure.

claims.claim: When a higher court overturns a verdict, it alters the dependency network that sustains the verdict's legal being.
claims.source_quote: When a higher court overturns a verdict, it does not erase the words spoken but alters the dependency network that sustains their legal being.
claims.note: Asserts what ontologically occurs when a verdict is overturned—a change in the dependency network.

claims.claim: An overturned verdict persists as a historical record but ceases to exist as juridical truth.
claims.source_quote: The earlier verdict persists as a historical record but ceases to exist as juridical truth.
claims.note: Asserts two distinct ontological states of the overturned verdict: persistence as historical record and non-existence as juridical truth.

claims.claim: The trier of fact occupies the apex of law's epistemic hierarchy.
claims.source_quote: In this way, the trier of fact occupies the apex of law's epistemic hierarchy: it is the institution's capacity for meta-recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a positional/relational property of the trier of fact within the epistemic hierarchy.

claims.claim: The trier of fact is the institution's capacity for meta-recognition.
claims.source_quote: the trier of fact occupies the apex of law's epistemic hierarchy: it is the institution's capacity for meta-recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a functional identity/role of the trier of fact.

claims.claim: The judge is a role continuant whose being depends on the institution of the judiciary, procedural framework, and public recognition.
claims.source_quote: As a role continuant, the judge's being depends on the institution of the judiciary, the procedural framework of adjudication, and the recognition of the public.
claims.note: Classifies the judge as a role continuant and asserts its dependence relations.

claims.claim: The judge realizes his role through occurrents of hearing, evaluating, and issuing judgment.
claims.source_quote: The judge realizes this role through occurrents of hearing, evaluating, and issuing judgment.
claims.note: Asserts a realization relation between the judge's role and specific occurrents.

claims.claim: Each judicial act (hearing, evaluation, judgment) functions as a recognition event.
claims.source_quote: Each of these acts functions as a recognition event: the hearing transforms evidence into deliberative content; evaluation transforms deliberation into finding; judgment transforms finding into legal fact.
claims.note: Asserts the functional kind of each judicial act.

claims.claim: The hearing transforms evidence into deliberative content.
claims.source_quote: the hearing transforms evidence into deliberative content; evaluation transforms deliberation into finding; judgment transforms finding into legal fact.
claims.note: Asserts a transformation relation as the function of the hearing occurrent.

claims.claim: Evaluation transforms deliberation into finding.
claims.source_quote: the hearing transforms evidence into deliberative content; evaluation transforms deliberation into finding; judgment transforms finding into legal fact.
claims.note: Asserts a transformation relation as the function of the evaluation occurrent.

claims.claim: Judgment transforms finding into legal fact.
claims.source_quote: the hearing transforms evidence into deliberative content; evaluation transforms deliberation into finding; judgment transforms finding into legal fact.
claims.note: Asserts a transformation relation as the function of the judgment occurrent.

claims.claim: The authority of each judicial transformation derives from the institutional continuant of the court.
claims.source_quote: The authority of each transformation derives from the institutional continuant of the court, which maintains the coherence of recognition across time and cases.
claims.note: Asserts a derivation/dependence relation between transformative authority and the court as institutional continuant.

claims.claim: The judge's cognition is ontologically subsumed by the collective recognition that sustains it.
claims.source_quote: The judge's cognition, while individual, is ontologically subsumed by the collective recognition that sustains it.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological subsumption relation between individual cognition and collective recognition.

claims.claim: The jury is a collective epistemic structure.
claims.source_quote: The jury, by contrast, represents the trier of fact as a collective epistemic structure.
claims.note: Classifies the jury as a kind of entity (collective epistemic structure).

claims.claim: The jury's being is an emergent dependent continuant of deliberation.
claims.source_quote: The jury's being is not the aggregate of its members' cognitions but the emergent dependent continuant of deliberation, a single collective role realized through interaction and institutional recognition.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological kind of the jury's being.

claims.claim: The jury exists only as a body constituted by the court.
claims.source_quote: The jury exists only as a body constituted by the court, guided by its instructions, and dissolved upon verdict.
claims.note: Asserts the dependence of the jury's existence on the court.

claims.claim: The jury is a temporally bounded institution—a transient continuant.
claims.source_quote: Ontologically, the jury is a temporally bounded institution: a transient continuant whose sole function is to transform evidential relations into the singular fact of a verdict.
claims.note: Classifies the jury as a transient continuant and asserts its temporal boundedness.

claims.claim: The jury's sole function is to transform evidential relations into the singular fact of a verdict.
claims.source_quote: a transient continuant whose sole function is to transform evidential relations into the singular fact of a verdict.
claims.note: Asserts a functional property of the jury as an institution.

claims.claim: Juridical truth is a process of realization, not a static correspondence.
claims.source_quote: Both forms of the trier of fact, judicial and jury-based, demonstrate that juridical truth is a process of realization, not a static correspondence.
claims.note: Asserts a positive ontological characterization of juridical truth.

claims.claim: Verdicts rendered by unauthorized tribunals, corrupt judges, or improperly constituted juries lack legal existence.
claims.source_quote: This explains why verdicts rendered by unauthorized tribunals, corrupt judges, or improperly constituted juries lack legal existence.
claims.note: Asserts that certain verdicts lack a specific kind of existence.

claims.claim: Once rendered by a recognized trier of fact, the verdict becomes part of the enduring ontology of the legal system.
claims.source_quote: Once rendered by a recognized trier of fact, the verdict becomes part of the enduring ontology of the legal system. It persists as an institutional fact recorded in registries, cited in precedent, and invoked in future deliberations.
claims.note: Asserts the verdict's membership in and persistence within the legal system's ontology.

claims.claim: Each verdict becomes evidence for future fact-finding.
claims.source_quote: each verdict becomes evidence for future fact-finding, integrating epistemic acts into the temporal fabric of legal being.
claims.note: Asserts a relational role of the verdict in the ongoing legal system.

claims.claim: Verdicts are nodes in a continuous network of recognition linking past and future acts of institutional cognition.
claims.source_quote: verdicts are not endpoints but nodes in a continuous network of recognition linking past and future acts of institutional cognition.
claims.note: Asserts the structural role/kind of verdicts within the network of legal recognition.

claims.claim: The trial is an occurrent that realizes dependent continuants including roles, functions, and procedural norms.
claims.source_quote: From the standpoint of Basic Formal Ontology (BFO), the trial is an occurrent that realizes several dependent continuants simultaneously: the roles of trial judge, jury, counsel, and witness; the functions of adjudication and defense; and the procedural norms that define what counts as valid evidence and reasoning.
claims.note: Classifies the trial as an occurrent and asserts its realization relations to multiple dependent continuants.

claims.claim: The trial functions as a realization event for the entire epistemic architecture of law.
claims.source_quote: The trial thus functions as a realization event for the entire epistemic architecture of law.
claims.note: Asserts the functional role of the trial as a realization event.

claims.claim: The trial is the ontological space in which recognition, evidence, and authority converge to produce determinate facts.
claims.source_quote: It is the ontological space in which recognition, evidence, and authority converge to produce determinate facts.
claims.note: Asserts a property/role of the trial as the site of convergence producing determinate facts.

claims.claim: Juridical truth is institutionally realized coherence, distinct from metaphysical or scientific truth.
claims.source_quote: What emerges from this process is not 'truth' in the metaphysical or scientific sense but a distinct ontological mode of truth: institutionally realized coherence.
claims.note: Asserts a positive ontological characterization of juridical truth as a distinct mode.

claims.claim: The trier of fact is the consciousness of law as a structure of being.
claims.source_quote: The trier of fact, in this sense, is the consciousness of law, not as a mind but as a structure of being that transforms the uncertain into the recognized and thereby keeps the legal world real.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological identity/role of the trier, though with the qualification 'not as a mind but as a structure of being'; direct ontological commitment is clear but metaphorical framing warrants medium confidence.

claims.claim: The dependent continuants realized in the trial exist as relational structures within the institutional continuant of the court.
claims.source_quote: These dependent continuants exist as relational structures within the institutional continuant of the court.
claims.note: Asserts the mode of existence and location of dependent continuants relative to the court.

claims.claim: Law in contexts of partial reform exists in a metastable state.
claims.source_quote: Law in these contexts exists in a metastable state: coherent enough to function but unable to resolve accumulated contradiction.
claims.note: Direct assertion about the ontological status of law under certain conditions.

claims.claim: Metastable legal conditions are ontologically precarious.
claims.source_quote: These conditions are ontologically precarious, for they depend on the constant exertion of compensatory effort.
claims.note: Author directly asserts an ontological property (precariousness) of these conditions.

claims.claim: Authoritarian rigidity and anomic collapse share a structural affinity.
claims.source_quote: Authoritarian rigidity and anomic collapse share a deeper structural affinity: both reflect breakdowns in the reflexivity of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a relational property (structural affinity) between two kinds of system failure.

claims.claim: Both authoritarianism and anomy are breakdowns in the reflexivity of recognition.
claims.source_quote: both reflect breakdowns in the reflexivity of recognition.
claims.note: Asserts a property shared by both kinds of failure—reflexivity breakdown.

claims.claim: In authoritarianism, reflexivity is suppressed and law cannot correct itself.
claims.source_quote: In authoritarianism, reflexivity is suppressed, law cannot see or correct itself.
claims.note: Author asserts a dispositional incapacity of law under authoritarianism.

claims.claim: In anomy, reflexivity is dispersed and law loses focus and authority.
claims.source_quote: In anomy, reflexivity is dispersed, law sees itself everywhere and nowhere, losing focus and authority.
claims.note: Author asserts a property of law under anomic conditions.

claims.claim: Once recognition ceases to be reflexive, the world of law ceases to be self-sustaining.
claims.source_quote: Once recognition ceases to be reflexive, either because it is monopolized or dissipated, the world of law ceases to be self-sustaining.
claims.note: Asserts a conditional ontological property: self-sustenance depends on reflexive recognition.

claims.claim: The loss of reflexive recognition produces ontological entropy in law.
claims.source_quote: What follows is ontological entropy: the gradual decay of coherence and the reversion of social life to brute relations of power, habit, or force.
claims.note: Author asserts that a specific ontological process (entropy) follows the loss of reflexivity.

claims.claim: In authoritarian systems, the legal order becomes performative rather than functional.
claims.source_quote: The legal order becomes performative rather than functional, mimicking coherence through procedural spectacle.
claims.note: Asserts a property (performative, not functional) of law under authoritarian conditions.

claims.claim: Citizens in decaying legal systems no longer experience law as a stable framework of meaning.
claims.source_quote: Citizens no longer experience law as a stable framework of meaning but as either a façade or a void.
claims.note: Asserts how subjects relate to law under pathological conditions—a relational/experiential ontological claim.

claims.claim: Authoritarian rigidity embodies the moral failure of closure.
claims.source_quote: Authoritarian rigidity embodies the moral failure of closure, the refusal to acknowledge contradiction or to recognize the autonomy of others.
claims.note: Asserts a property (moral failure of closure) of authoritarian rigidity.

claims.claim: Anomic collapse embodies the moral failure of dissolution.
claims.source_quote: Anomic collapse embodies the moral failure of dissolution, the abandonment of shared recognition and the retreat into self-interest or despair.
claims.note: Asserts a property (moral failure of dissolution) of anomic collapse.

claims.claim: Both authoritarianism and anomy are failures of relational being.
claims.source_quote: Both are failures of relational being, in which the capacity for recognition that constitutes law is lost.
claims.note: Asserts a kind-membership claim: both pathologies are instances of failures of relational being.

claims.claim: Recognition constitutes law.
claims.source_quote: the capacity for recognition that constitutes law is lost.
claims.note: Direct ontological claim about the constitutive relation between recognition and law.

claims.claim: Law endures by sustaining the machinery of repair rather than eliminating contradiction.
claims.source_quote: Law endures not by eliminating contradiction but by sustaining the delicate machinery of repair.
claims.note: Asserts a functional/dispositional property of law's persistence.

claims.claim: Repair is the ontological process by which contradiction debt is absorbed and coherence restored.
claims.source_quote: Repair, as developed throughout this work, is the ontological process by which contradiction debt is absorbed and coherence restored within law's relational architecture.
claims.note: Directly defines repair as an ontological process with specific function—absorption and restoration.

claims.claim: Obligations, roles, and rights are dependent continuants that structure law's being.
claims.source_quote: Dependent Continuants (Obligations, Roles, Rights): enduring relations that structure law's being.
claims.note: Asserts the ontological category (dependent continuants) and function of these entities.

claims.claim: Courts, legislatures, and administrative bodies are institutional continuants that bear repair capacity.
claims.source_quote: Institutional Continuants (Courts, Legislatures, Administrative Bodies): bearers of repair capacity.
claims.note: Asserts that these institutions are a kind (institutional continuants) with a property (bearing repair capacity).

claims.claim: Adjudication, amendment, and reinterpretation are repair occurrents that realign dependencies.
claims.source_quote: Repair Occurrents (Adjudication, Amendment, Reinterpretation): mechanisms that realign dependencies.
claims.note: Asserts ontological category (occurrents) and function of these processes.

claims.claim: Repair is a self-referential loop that maintains the identity of law across change.
claims.source_quote: repair is not a one-time correction but a recurring ontological process, a self-referential loop that maintains the identity of law across change.
claims.note: Asserts a property (self-referential, identity-maintaining) of the repair process.

claims.claim: Law has the capacity to remain itself by continuously reconstituting its own coherence.
claims.source_quote: embodying what may be called reflexive persistence: the ability of law to remain itself by continuously reconstituting its own coherence.
claims.note: Author introduces 'reflexive persistence' as a property of law; medium confidence due to the hedging phrase 'what may be called.'

claims.claim: Contradiction debt accumulates when recognition is delayed, increasing systemic fragility.
claims.source_quote: Ontological implication: delayed recognition allows contradiction debt to accumulate, increasing systemic fragility.
claims.note: Author explicitly labels this an ontological implication and asserts it as a causal/constitutive claim.

claims.claim: Repair efficiency measures the system's capacity to realign dependencies without structural rupture.
claims.source_quote: Ontologically, RE measures the system's capacity to realign dependencies without structural rupture.
claims.note: Author asserts an ontological property of the repair efficiency metric.

claims.claim: The trial is a realization event for the entire epistemic architecture of law.
claims.source_quote: The trial thus functions as a realization event for the entire epistemic architecture of law.
claims.note: The author asserts that the trial bears the relation of realization to the epistemic architecture of law — an ontological relational claim.

claims.claim: The trial is an ontological space in which recognition, evidence, and authority converge.
