claims.claim: Each legal rule is a crystallized relation—an encoded recognition linking one being to another.
claims.source_quote: Students learn to see that each legal rule is a crystallized relation, an encoded recognition linking one being to another.
claims.note: Author endorses this ontological characterization of legal rules as relations/recognitions.

claims.claim: Law is a living system of being.
claims.source_quote: Law, when taught ontologically, is no longer treated as a set of rules to memorize or cases to categorize, but as a living system of being.
claims.note: Author asserts this as the correct ontological characterization of law, not merely a pedagogical stance.

claims.claim: Law is the structure of being-with.
claims.source_quote: grounding each experiment in the metaphysical understanding that law is the structure of being-with.
claims.note: Asserts an ontological identity claim about law's fundamental nature.

claims.claim: Participating in law is participating in the maintenance of being.
claims.source_quote: To participate in the law is to participate in the maintenance of being.
claims.note: Asserts a participation relation between legal actors and the ontological domain of being.

claims.claim: Every act of drafting, judging, or interpreting law is an intervention in the ontology of the social world.
claims.source_quote: Every act of drafting, judging, or interpreting is an act of construction, an intervention in the ontology of the social world.
claims.note: Asserts that legal acts bear the relation of intervention to the ontology of the social world.

claims.claim: Law's endurance depends on its capacity to sustain coherence through time, not on enforcement alone.
claims.source_quote: They learn that law's endurance depends not on enforcement alone but on its capacity to sustain coherence through time.
claims.note: Asserts a dependency relation between law's endurance and coherence-sustaining capacity.

claims.claim: Recognition relations sustain institutions.
claims.source_quote: Which recognition relations sustain this institution, and where are they failing?
claims.note: The question format is used pedagogically, but the author's framing commits to recognition relations as sustaining institutions.

claims.claim: Justice is the inner logic of law, not external to it.
claims.source_quote: They come to see that justice is not external to the law but its inner logic, its measure of coherence with the world it orders.
claims.note: The author asserts a property/relation of justice to law in his own voice.

claims.claim: Unjust institutions are ontologically incoherent.
claims.source_quote: When institutions become unjust, it is not only because they have violated moral norms, but because they have become ontologically incoherent, detached from the recognition that once sustained them.
claims.note: The author asserts a property of unjust institutions — ontological incoherence — as a positive claim.

claims.claim: Unjust institutions are detached from the recognition that once sustained them.
claims.source_quote: When institutions become unjust, it is not only because they have violated moral norms, but because they have become ontologically incoherent, detached from the recognition that once sustained them.
claims.note: Author asserts a relational property of unjust institutions regarding recognition.

claims.claim: Rights, duties, and institutions are mechanisms through which people live together.
claims.source_quote: Students learn that the abstractions of law, rights, duties, institutions, are not distant constructs but the very mechanisms through which people live together.
claims.note: Author asserts the ontological role/function of legal abstractions.

claims.claim: Contract law is the formalization of reciprocal obligations.
claims.source_quote: Contract law as the formalization of reciprocal obligations.
claims.note: Author asserts the ontological character/function of contract law.

claims.claim: Property law manages dependent continuants (ownership relations) within institutional continuants.
claims.source_quote: Property law as the management of dependent continuants (ownership relations) within institutional continuants (registries, markets, states).
claims.note: Author asserts the ontological function and structure of property law.

claims.claim: Constitutional law is the meta-ontology of recognition governing coherence of all institutional relations.
claims.source_quote: Constitutional law as the meta-ontology of recognition, governing the coherence of all other institutional relations.
claims.note: Author asserts a kind-identity and function for constitutional law.

claims.claim: We exist only in relation.
claims.source_quote: It teaches that every courtroom, constitution, and code is an expression of the same ontological truth: that we exist only in relation, and that justice is the name we give to the coherence of those relations.
claims.note: Author asserts a fundamental ontological claim about human existence as relational.

claims.claim: Justice is the coherence of the relations through which we exist.
claims.source_quote: that we exist only in relation, and that justice is the name we give to the coherence of those relations.
claims.note: Author asserts an ontological definition/property of justice.

claims.claim: Every courtroom, constitution, and code is an expression of recognition structures.
claims.source_quote: It invites those who study law to look beyond the surface of institutions and perceive the structures of recognition that give them life.
claims.note: Author asserts that recognition structures are what give institutions life — a relational ontological claim.

claims.claim: Law is a living structure requiring continuous stewardship.
claims.source_quote: Such questions train future jurists to think beyond reform toward design, to treat law as a living structure requiring continuous stewardship.
claims.note: Author asserts a property of law (living, requiring stewardship), though framed pedagogically; still an ontological commitment about law's nature.

claims.claim: Justice is the living coherence of being-with.
claims.source_quote: Their task is to sustain justice as the living coherence of being-with.
claims.note: Author asserts an ontological characterization of justice.

claims.claim: Structural ontology is an epistemic infrastructure for the study of justice.
claims.source_quote: In this sense, structural ontology offers not just a theory of law but a new epistemic infrastructure for the study of justice itself.
claims.note: Author asserts a functional/ontological role for structural ontology.

claims.claim: Law is the medium of justice.
claims.source_quote: law regains its unity with philosophy and its role as the medium of justice.
claims.note: Author asserts a relational role of law with respect to justice.

claims.claim: Law is the architecture of justice — a living, dynamic structure.
claims.source_quote: It becomes, once again, what it has always been at its highest sense: the architecture of justice, the living, dynamic structure through which human beings, together, create and sustain the possibility of a coherent world.
claims.note: Author asserts the ontological kind and properties of law.

claims.claim: Human beings together create and sustain a coherent world through law.
claims.source_quote: the living, dynamic structure through which human beings, together, create and sustain the possibility of a coherent world.
claims.note: Author asserts a relational ontological claim about the function of law in human collective existence.

claims.claim: Law is the architecture of justice.
claims.source_quote: It becomes, once again, what it has always been at its highest sense: the architecture of justice, the living, dynamic structure through which human beings, together, create and sustain the possibility of a coherent world.
claims.note: The author asserts a property/role of law: that it is (at its highest) the architecture of justice.

claims.claim: Law is a living, dynamic structure.
claims.source_quote: the living, dynamic structure through which human beings, together, create and sustain the possibility of a coherent world.
claims.note: The author attributes the property of being a living, dynamic structure to law.

claims.claim: Law is the medium through which human beings create and sustain a coherent world.
claims.source_quote: the living, dynamic structure through which human beings, together, create and sustain the possibility of a coherent world.
claims.note: The author asserts a functional/relational role of law with respect to social reality and human beings.

claims.claim: Law is the medium of justice.
claims.source_quote: law regains its unity with philosophy and its role as the medium of justice.
claims.note: The author asserts a role/function of law: it is the medium of justice.

claims.claim: Law has a unity with philosophy.
claims.source_quote: law regains its unity with philosophy and its role as the medium of justice.
claims.note: The author asserts a relational property between law and philosophy (unity), endorsing this as a recovered truth.

claims.claim: Social order arises from coherent recognition, obligation fulfillment, and institutional repair.
claims.source_quote: Social order is not imposed solely by coercion but arises from coherent recognition, obligation fulfillment, and institutional repair.
claims.note: Direct assertion about the causal/constitutive basis of social order — an ontological claim about what social order is produced by.

claims.claim: Social order is produced by sustained legal and moral structures.
claims.source_quote: produced by sustained legal and moral structures. Social order is not imposed solely by coercion but arises from coherent recognition, obligation fulfillment, and institutional repair.
claims.note: Asserts a productive/causal relation between legal/moral structures and social order.

claims.claim: Law is a relational, layered architecture of continuants, occurrents, and recognition structures.
claims.source_quote: An approach that understands law as a relational, layered architecture of continuants, occurrents, and recognition structures, rather than as a mere system of rules or commands.
claims.note: The author defines law's ontological character as a structural architecture, not merely rules or commands.

claims.claim: Agent is a subkind of Continuant.
claims.source_quote: law:Agent a owl:Class ; rdfs:subClassOf bfo:Continuant .
claims.note: Formal ontological classification: Agent is declared a subclass of BFO Continuant.

claims.claim: Institution is a subkind of Continuant.
claims.source_quote: law:Institution a owl:Class ; rdfs:subClassOf bfo:Continuant ; rdfs:comment "Aggregated continuant composed of interrelated roles and norms."
claims.note: Formal ontological classification: Institution is declared a subclass of BFO Continuant.

claims.claim: Institution is an aggregated continuant composed of interrelated roles and norms.
claims.source_quote: rdfs:comment "Aggregated continuant composed of interrelated roles and norms."
claims.note: Asserts the internal composition/structure of Institution as an ontological entity.

claims.claim: Role is a subkind of RealizableEntity.
claims.source_quote: law:Role a owl:Class ; rdfs:subClassOf bfo:RealizableEntity .
claims.note: Formal ontological classification: Role is declared a subclass of BFO RealizableEntity.

claims.claim: Obligation is a subkind of DependentContinuant.
claims.source_quote: law:Obligation a owl:Class ; rdfs:subClassOf bfo:DependentContinuant ;
claims.note: Formal ontological classification: Obligation is declared a subclass of BFO DependentContinuant.

claims.claim: Obligation is a dependent continuant that constrains an agent's possible actions.
claims.source_quote: rdfs:comment "A dependent continuant that constrains an agent's possible actions."
claims.note: Asserts a property/function of Obligation as an ontological entity.

claims.claim: Recognition is a subkind of RelationalQuality.
claims.source_quote: law:Recognition a owl:Class ; rdfs:subClassOf bfo:RelationalQuality .
claims.note: Formal ontological classification: Recognition is declared a subclass of BFO RelationalQuality.

claims.claim: RepairProcess is a subkind of Process.
claims.source_quote: law:RepairProcess a owl:Class ; rdfs:subClassOf bfo:Process .
claims.note: Formal ontological classification: RepairProcess is declared a subclass of BFO Process.

claims.claim: Agents bear roles.
claims.source_quote: law:bearsRole a owl:ObjectProperty ; rdfs:domain law:Agent ; rdfs:range law:Role .
claims.note: Asserts a formal relational property between Agent and Role.

claims.claim: Institutions confer recognition on agents.
claims.source_quote: law:confersRecognition a owl:ObjectProperty ; rdfs:domain law:Institution ; rdfs:range law:Agent .
claims.note: Asserts a formal relational property between Institution and Agent.

claims.claim: RepairProcesses realize obligations.
claims.source_quote: law:realizesObligation a owl:ObjectProperty ; rdfs:domain law:RepairProcess ; rdfs:range law:Obligation .
claims.note: Asserts a realization relation between RepairProcess and Obligation.

claims.claim: Agents sustain institutions (through recognition).
claims.source_quote: law:sustainsRecognition a owl:ObjectProperty ; rdfs:domain law:Agent ; rdfs:range law:Institution .
claims.note: Asserts a formal relational property between Agent and Institution.

claims.claim: CourtOfLaw is an individual Institution.
claims.source_quote: law:CourtOfLaw a law:Institution .
claims.note: Asserts an individual of the Institution kind.

claims.claim: Judge is an individual Agent.
claims.source_quote: law:Judge a law:Agent .
claims.note: Asserts an individual of the Agent kind.

claims.claim: JudicialRole is an individual Role.
claims.source_quote: law:JudicialRole a law:Role .
claims.note: Asserts an individual of the Role kind.

claims.claim: Adjudication is an individual RepairProcess.
claims.source_quote: law:Adjudication a law:RepairProcess .
claims.note: Asserts an individual of the RepairProcess kind.

claims.claim: The Judge bears the JudicialRole.
claims.source_quote: law:Judge law:bearsRole law:JudicialRole .
claims.note: Asserts a specific relational fact between two individuals.

claims.claim: The CourtOfLaw confers recognition on the Judge.
claims.source_quote: law:CourtOfLaw law:confersRecognition law:Judge .
claims.note: Asserts a specific relational fact between two individuals.

claims.claim: Adjudication realizes LegalObligation.
claims.source_quote: law:Adjudication law:realizesObligation law:LegalObligation .
claims.note: Asserts a realization relation between two specific individuals.

claims.claim: Recognition, obligation, and repair are entities expressible in a formal ontology.
claims.source_quote: showing how abstract relations (recognition, obligation, repair) become computable entities for simulation and verification.
claims.note: The author asserts these abstract relations have ontological status as computable entities, not merely as concepts.
